The majority of our consumer </div><div id="a3060" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:294px;">loans are short-term and have fixed rates of interest that are priced<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>based on current market interest rates and the financial </div><div id="a3104" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:309px;">strength of the borrower. Our policy<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>establishes maximum debt-to-income ratios, minimum credit scores, and includes<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>guidelines </div><div id="a3140" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:324px;">for verification of applicants&#8217; income and receipt of credit reports. </div><div id="a3161" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:355px;">Expansion of Business </div><div id="a3164" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:386px;">See Item 7.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Financial Condition and Results of Operations under the section captioned </div><div id="a3166" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:401px;">&#8220;Business Overview&#8221; for discussion related to the expansion of our<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Business. </div><div id="a3171" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:432px;">Competition </div><div id="a3174" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:462px;">We face significant<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>competition in our market areas. We<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>compete against a wide range of banking and nonbanking institutions </div><div id="a3176" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:478px;">including banks, savings and loan associations, credit unions, money market<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>funds, mutual fund advisory companies, mortgage </div><div id="a3177" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:493px;">banking companies, investment banking companies, insurance agencies and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>companies, securities firms, brokerage firms, </div><div id="a3178" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:508px;">financial technology firms, personal and commercial finance companies<div style="display:inline-block;width:2px">&#160;</div>,<div style="display:inline-block;width:3px">&#160;</div>peer-to-peer lending businesses and other types of </div><div id="a3188" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:524px;">financial institutions. In addition to traditional competitors, we also face increasing<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>competition from a rapidly expanding group </div><div id="a3191" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:539px;">of nontraditional financial service providers. These include established and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>emerging wealth technology companies </div><div id="a3192" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:554px;">(&#8220;wealthtechs&#8221;), financial technology companies (&#8220;fintechs&#8221;), technology<div style="display:inline-block;width:2px">&#160;</div>-enabled lenders, digital-only banks, crowdfunding </div><div id="a3197" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:570px;">platforms, and mobile-based payment applications. These firms often<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>leverage advanced technologies, agile product development </div><div id="a3200" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:585px;">cycles, and streamlined digital interfaces that allow them to deliver certain<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>financial products and services&#8212;such as unsecured </div><div id="a3203" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:600px;">consumer loans, small business working-capital loans, digital wallets, and peer-to-peer<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>payments&#8212;more quickly or conveniently </div><div id="a3212" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:616px;">than traditional banking institutions. Some fintech competitors operate<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>with lower overhead and, in some cases, are subject to </div><div id="a3214" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:631px;">fewer regulatory requirements than banks and bank holding companies.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>This can allow them to offer competitive pricing, faster </div><div id="a3216" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:646px;">decision making or funding, and simplified user experiences. Some<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of our competitors are larger financial institutions with greater </div><div id="a3218" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:662px;">resources and, as such, may have higher lending limits and may offer<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>other services that are not provided by us. Industry </div><div id="a3220" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:677px;">consolidation also intensifies competition in our markets. Mergers<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>among financial institutions have created larger, </div><div id="a3221" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:692px;">better-capitalized, and more geographically diverse<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>competitors with expanded digital capabilities and broader product sets. These </div><div id="a3224" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:708px;">institutions may be better positioned to make significant investments in technology,<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>marketing, and infrastructure, which can </div><div id="a3226" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:723px;">enhance their ability to compete for both clients and talent.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>However, we believe that the larger<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>financial institutions are less </div><div id="a3229" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:738px;">familiar with the markets in which we operate and typically target<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a different client base. We<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>also believe clients who bank at </div><div id="a3231" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:754px;">community banks tend to prefer the relationship style service of community<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>banks compared to larger banks and financial </div><div id="a3232" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:769px;">services companies. </div><div id="a3235" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:800px;">As a result, we expect to be able to effectively compete in our markets<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>with larger financial institutions through providing </div><div id="a3236" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:815px;">superior client service and leveraging our knowledge and experience<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in providing banking products and services in our market </div><div id="a3237" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:830px;">areas. See Item 1A. Risk Factors under the section captioned &#8220;Our future success is dependent<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>on our ability to compete </div><div id="a3238" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:846px;">effectively in the highly competitive banking and financial<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>services industry&#8221; for further discussion related to the competitive </div><div id="a3240" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:861px;">environment in which we operate. </div><div id="a3243" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:892px;">Our primary market area consists of 21 counties in Florida, six counties in Georgia,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and one county in Alabama. Most of Florida&#8217;s </div><div id="a3245" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:907px;">major banking concerns have a presence in Leon County,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>where our main office is located.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Our Leon County deposits totaled </div><div id="a3246" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:922px;">$1.195 billion, or 32.6% of our consolidated deposits at December<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>31, 2025. </div></div>

These include, but are not </div><div id="a4236" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:278px;">limited to, the Securities and Exchange Commission (&#8220;SEC&#8221;), the Financial<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Industry Regulatory Authority,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>federal and state </div><div id="a4237" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:294px;">banking regulators, and various state regulators of insurance and brokerage activities. </div><div id="a4240" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:324px;">Violations of laws and regulations,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or other unsafe and unsound practices, may result in regulatory agencies imposing<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>fines or </div><div id="a4242" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:340px;">penalties, cease and desist orders, or taking other enforcement actions. Under<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>certain circumstances, these agencies may enforce </div><div id="a4244" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:355px;">these remedies directly against officers, directors, employees, and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>other parties participating in the affairs of a bank or bank </div><div id="a4246" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:370px;">holding company.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Like all bank holding companies, we are regulated extensively under federal and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>state law. Under federal and </div><div id="a4248" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:386px;">state laws and regulations pertaining to the safety and soundness of insured depository<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>institutions, state banking regulators, the </div><div id="a4250" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:401px;">Federal Reserve, and separately the FDIC as the insurer of bank deposits have the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>authority to compel or restrict certain actions </div><div id="a4252" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:416px;">on our part if they determine that we have insufficient capital or<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>other resources, or are otherwise operating in a manner that may </div><div id="a4254" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:432px;">be deemed to be inconsistent with safe and sound banking practices. Under<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>this authority, our regulators<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>can require us or our </div><div id="a4256" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:447px;">subsidiaries to enter into informal or formal supervisory agreements, including<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>board resolutions, memoranda of understanding, </div><div id="a4258" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:462px;">written agreements, and consent or cease and desist orders pursuant to which<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>we would be required to take identified corrective </div><div id="a4260" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:478px;">actions to address cited concerns and to refrain from taking certain actions. </div><div id="a4263" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:508px;">If we become subject to and are unable to comply with the terms of any regulatory<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>actions or directives, supervisory agreements </div><div id="a4265" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:524px;">or orders, then we could become subject to additional, heightened supervisory<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>actions and orders, possibly including prompt </div><div id="a4266" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:539px;">corrective action restrictions and/or other regulatory actions, including<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>prohibitions on the payment of dividends on our common </div><div id="a4268" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:554px;">stock and preferred stock. If our regulators were to take such supervisory actions,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>then we could, among other things, become </div><div id="a4270" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:570px;">subject to significant restrictions on our ability to develop any new business, as well as restrictions<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>on our existing business, and </div><div id="a4272" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:585px;">we could be required to raise additional capital, dispose of certain assets and liabilities within<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a prescribed period of time, or both. </div><div id="a4274" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:600px;">The terms of any such action could have a material negative effect<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>on our business, reputation, operating flexibility,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>financial </div><div id="a4276" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:616px;">condition, and the value of our capital stock. </div></div>

<div id="Page13" style="background-color:RGB(255, 255, 255);position:relative;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;overflow:hidden;border-style:solid;border-width:thin;border-color:RGB(198, 198, 198);page-break-after:always;width:816px;height:1056px;">
<div id="a4280" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:404px;top:1022px;">13 </div><div id="a4282" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:48px;">Permitted Activities </div><div id="a4287" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:79px;">As a financial holding company,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>we are permitted to engage directly or indirectly in a broader range of activities than<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>those </div><div id="a4329" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:94px;">permitted for a bank holding company that has not elected to be a financial holding<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>company. Bank holding companies<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>are </div><div id="a4369" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:110px;">generally restricted to engaging in the business of banking, managing,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or controlling banks and certain other activities determined </div><div id="a4405" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:125px;">by the Federal Reserve to be closely related to banking. Financial holding companies<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>may also engage in activities that are </div><div id="a4445" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:140px;">considered to be financial in nature, as well as those incidental or,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>if determined by the Federal Reserve, complementary to </div><div id="a4485" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:156px;">financial activities. If the Bank ceases to be &#8220;well capitalized&#8221; or &#8220;well managed&#8221;<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>under applicable regulatory standards, or if the </div><div id="a4525" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:171px;">Bank receives a rating of less than satisfactory under the CRA, the Federal<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Reserve may, among other<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>things, place limitations on </div><div id="a4567" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:186px;">our ability to conduct these broader financial activities or,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>if the deficiencies persist, require us to divest the banking subsidiary or </div><div id="a4609" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:202px;">the businesses engaged in activities permissible only for financial holding<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>companies. </div><div id="a4632" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:232px;">In addition, the Federal Reserve has the power to order a bank holding<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>company or its subsidiaries to terminate any nonbanking </div><div id="a4674" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:248px;">activity or terminate its ownership or control of any nonbank subsidiary<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>when it has reasonable cause to believe that continuation </div><div id="a4714" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:263px;">of such activity or such ownership or control constitutes a serious risk to the financial<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>safety, soundness, or stability of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>any bank </div><div id="a4758" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:278px;">subsidiary of that bank holding company.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>As further described below, each of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the Company and the Bank is well-capitalized </div><div id="a4798" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:294px;">under applicable regulatory standards as of December 31, 2025,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and the Bank has an overall rating of &#8220;Satisfactory&#8221; in its most </div><div id="a4840" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:309px;">recent CRA evaluation. </div><div id="a4847" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:340px;">Source of Strength Obligations </div><div id="a4856" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:370px;">A bank holding company,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>such as us, is required to act as a source of financial and managerial strength to its subsidiary bank.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>The </div><div id="a4905" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:386px;">term &#8220;source of financial strength&#8221; means the ability of a company,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>such as us, that directly or indirectly owns or controls an </div><div id="a4949" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:401px;">insured depository institution, such as the Bank, to provide financial<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>assistance to such insured depository institution in the event </div><div id="a4987" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:416px;">of financial distress. The appropriate federal banking agency for<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the depository institution (in the case of the Bank, this agency is </div><div id="a5029" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:432px;">the Federal Reserve) may require reports from us to assess our ability<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to serve as a source of strength and to enforce compliance </div><div id="a5075" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:447px;">with the source of strength requirements by requiring us to provide financial<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>assistance to the Bank in the event of financial </div><div id="a5117" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:462px;">distress. If we were to enter bankruptcy or become subject to the orderly<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>liquidation process established by the Dodd-Frank Wall </div><div id="a5159" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:478px;">Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (&#8220;Dodd-Frank Act&#8221;),<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>any commitment by us to a federal bank regulatory agency to </div><div id="a5199" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:493px;">maintain the capital of the Bank would be assumed by the bankruptcy<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>trustee or the FDIC, as appropriate, and entitled to a </div><div id="a5243" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:508px;">priority of payment. In addition, the FDIC provides that any insured<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>depository institution generally will be liable for any loss </div><div id="a5283" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:524px;">incurred by the FDIC in connection with the default of, or any assistance provided<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>by the FDIC to, a commonly controlled insured </div><div id="a5327" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:539px;">depository institution. The Bank is an FDIC-insured depository institution<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and thus subject to these requirements. </div><div id="a5360" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:570px;">Acquisitions </div><div id="a5363" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:600px;">The BHC Act permits acquisitions of banks by bank holding companies,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>such that we and any other bank holding company, </div><div id="a5403" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:616px;">whether located in Florida or elsewhere, may acquire a bank located in<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>any other state, subject to certain deposit-percentage, age </div><div id="a5445" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:631px;">of bank charter requirements, and other restrictions. The BHC Act requires that<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a bank holding company obtain the prior approval </div><div id="a5485" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:646px;">of the Federal Reserve before (i) acquiring direct or indirect ownership<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or control of more than 5% of the voting shares of any </div><div id="a5531" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:662px;">additional bank or bank holding company,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>(ii) taking any action that causes an additional bank or bank holding company<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to </div><div id="a5571" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:677px;">become a subsidiary of the bank holding company,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or (iii) merging or consolidating with any other bank<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>holding company. The </div><div id="a5611" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:692px;">Federal Reserve may not approve any such transaction that would result<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in a monopoly or would be in furtherance of any </div><div id="a5653" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:708px;">combination or conspiracy to monopolize or attempt to monopolize the business<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of banking in any section of the United States, or </div><div id="a5695" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:723px;">the effect of which may be substantially to lessen competition<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or to tend to create a monopoly in any section of the country,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or </div><div id="a5743" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:738px;">that in any other manner would be in restraint of trade unless the anticompetitive<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>effects of the proposed transaction are clearly </div><div id="a5785" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:754px;">outweighed in the public interest by the probable effect of the transaction<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in meeting the convenience and needs of the community </div><div id="a5827" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:769px;">to be served. The Federal Reserve is also required to consider: (i) the financial and managerial<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>resources of the companies </div><div id="a5867" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:784px;">involved, including pro forma capital ratios; (ii) the risk to the stability of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the United States banking or financial system; (iii) the </div><div id="a5911" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:800px;">convenience and needs of the communities to be served, including performance<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>under the CRA; and (iv) the effectiveness of the </div><div id="a5951" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:815px;">company in combatting money laundering. </div><div id="a5962" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:846px;">Change in Control </div><div id="a5969" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:876px;">Federal law restricts the amount of voting stock of a bank holding company<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or a bank that a person may acquire without the prior </div><div id="a6017" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:892px;">approval of banking regulators. Under the Change in Bank Control<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Act and the regulations thereunder, a person or group<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>must </div><div id="a6057" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:907px;">give advance notice to the Federal Reserve before acquiring control<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of any bank holding company,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>such as the Company, or </div><div id="a6097" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:922px;">before acquiring control of any FDIC-insured bank, such as the Bank.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Upon receipt of such notice, the Federal Reserve may </div><div id="a6139" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:938px;">approve or disapprove the acquisition. The Change in Bank Control Act creates<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a rebuttable presumption of control if a person or </div><div id="a6181" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:953px;">group acquires the power to vote 10% or more of our outstanding<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>common stock.<div style="display:inline-block;width:3px">&#160;</div></div></div>

<div id="Page14" style="background-color:RGB(255, 255, 255);position:relative;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;overflow:hidden;border-style:solid;border-width:thin;border-color:RGB(198, 198, 198);page-break-after:always;width:816px;height:1056px;">
<div id="a6212" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:404px;top:1022px;">14 </div><div id="a6214" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:48px;">Under Florida law,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a person or entity proposing to directly or indirectly acquire control of a Florida chartered<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>bank must also </div><div id="a6256" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:64px;">obtain permission from the Florida Office of Financial<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Regulation (the &#8220;Florida OFR&#8221;). The Florida Statutes define &#8220;control&#8221;<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>as </div><div id="a6292" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:79px;">either (i) indirectly or directly owning, controlling or having power<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to vote 25% or more of the voting securities of a bank; (ii) </div><div id="a6338" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:94px;">controlling the election of a majority of directors of a bank; (iii) owning,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>controlling, or having power to vote 10% or more of the </div><div id="a6386" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:110px;">voting securities as well as directly or indirectly exercising a controlling<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>influence over management or policies of a bank; or (iv) </div><div id="a6428" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:125px;">as determined by the<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Florida OFR. These requirements will affect us because the Bank is chartered<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>under Florida law and </div><div id="a6468" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:140px;">changes in control of the Company are indirect changes in control<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of the Bank. </div><div id="a6497" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:171px;">The overall effect of such laws is to make it more difficult<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to acquire a bank holding company and a bank by tender offer or </div><div id="a6547" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:186px;">similar means than it might be to acquire control of another type of corporation.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Consequently, shareholders<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of the Company may </div><div id="a6587" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:202px;">be less likely to benefit from the rapid increases in stock prices that may result<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>from tender offers or similar efforts to acquire </div><div id="a6633" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:217px;">control of other companies. Investors should be aware of these requirements<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>when acquiring shares of our stock. </div><div id="a6668" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:248px;">Incentive Compensation </div><div id="a6673" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:278px;">The Dodd-Frank Act required the federal banking agencies and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the SEC to establish joint rules or guidelines for financial </div><div id="a6713" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:294px;">institutions with more than $1 billion in assets, such as us and the Bank,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>which prohibit incentive compensation arrangements that </div><div id="a6753" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:309px;">the agencies determine to encourage inappropriate risks by the institution.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>The federal banking agencies issued proposed rules in </div><div id="a6789" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:324px;">2011 and previously issued guidance<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>on sound incentive compensation policies. In 2016, the federal banking<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>agencies and the </div><div id="a6825" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:340px;">SEC proposed rules that would, depending upon the assets of the institution, directly<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>regulate incentive compensation </div><div id="a6857" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:355px;">arrangements and would require enhanced oversight and recordkeeping.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>As of December 31, 2025, these rules have not been </div><div id="a6893" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:370px;">implemented, although the SEC did adopt final rules implementing<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the clawback provisions of the Dodd-Frank Act in 2022. </div><div id="a6931" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:729px;top:370px;">We </div><div id="a6933" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:386px;">and the Bank have undertaken efforts to ensure that our<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>incentive compensation plans do not encourage inappropriate risks, </div><div id="a6969" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:401px;">consistent with three key principles - that incentive compensation arrangements<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>should appropriately balance risk and financial </div><div id="a7001" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:416px;">rewards, be compatible with effective controls and risk management,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and be supported by strong corporate governance. </div><div id="a7034" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:447px;">Source of Strength Obligations </div><div id="a7043" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:478px;">A bank holding company,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>such as us, is required to act as a source of financial and managerial strength to its subsidiary bank.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>The </div><div id="a7091" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:493px;">term &#8220;source of financial strength&#8221; means the ability of a company,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>such as us, that directly or indirectly owns or controls an </div><div id="a7135" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:508px;">insured depository institution, such as the Bank, to provide financial<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>assistance to such insured depository institution in the event </div><div id="a7173" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:524px;">of financial distress. The appropriate federal banking agency for<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the depository institution (in the case of the Bank, this agency is </div><div id="a7215" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:539px;">the Federal Reserve) may require reports from us to assess our ability<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to serve as a source of strength and to enforce compliance </div><div id="a7261" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:554px;">with the source of strength requirements by requiring us to provide financial<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>assistance to the Bank in the event of financial </div><div id="a7303" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:570px;">distress. If we were to enter bankruptcy or become subject to the orderly<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>liquidation process established by the Dodd-Frank Act, </div><div id="a7345" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:585px;">any commitment by us to a federal bank regulatory agency to maintain<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the capital of the Bank would be assumed by the </div><div id="a7389" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:600px;">bankruptcy trustee or the FDIC, as appropriate, and entitled to a priority<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of payment. In addition, the FDIC provides that any </div><div id="a7431" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:616px;">insured depository institution generally will be liable for any loss incurred<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>by the FDIC in connection with the default of, or any </div><div id="a7475" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:631px;">assistance provided by the FDIC to, a commonly controlled insured<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>depository institution. The Bank is an FDIC-insured </div><div id="a7511" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:646px;">depository institution and thus subject to these requirements. </div><div id="a7528" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:677px;">Capital Requirements<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a7534" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:708px;">We </div><div id="a7536" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:84px;top:708px;">and the Bank are required under federal law to maintain certain minimum<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>capital levels based on ratios of capital to total </div><div id="a7578" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:723px;">assets and capital to risk-weighted assets. The required capital ratios are minimums,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and the Federal Reserve may determine that a </div><div id="a7620" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:738px;">banking organization based on its size, complexity,<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>or risk profile must maintain a higher level of capital in order to operate in a </div><div id="a7666" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:754px;">safe and sound manner.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Risks such as concentration of credit risks and the risk arising from nontraditional activities,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>as well as the </div><div id="a7710" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:769px;">institution&#8217;s exposure<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to a decline in the economic value of its capital due to changes in interest rates, and an<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>institution&#8217;s ability </div><div id="a7754" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:784px;">to manage those risks, are important factors that are to be taken into account<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in assessing an institution&#8217;s overall<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>capital adequacy. </div><div id="a7796" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:800px;">The following is a brief description of the relevant provisions of these capital<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>rules and their potential impact on our capital levels. </div><div id="a7841" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:830px;">We </div><div id="a7843" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:84px;top:830px;">and the Bank are subject to the following risk-based capital ratios: a CET1 risk-based<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>capital ratio, a Tier 1 risk-based capital </div><div id="a7891" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:846px;">ratio, which includes CET1 and additional Tier<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>1 capital, and a total risk-based capital ratio, which includes Tier<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>1 and Tier 2 </div><div id="a7937" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:861px;">capital. CET1 is primarily comprised of the sum of common stock instruments<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and related surplus net of treasury stock plus </div><div id="a7977" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:876px;">retained earnings less certain adjustments and deductions, including<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>with respect to goodwill, intangible assets, mortgage </div><div id="a8007" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:892px;">servicing assets, and deferred tax assets subject to temporary timing differences.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Additional Tier 1 capital is primarily comprised </div><div id="a8043" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:907px;">of noncumulative perpetual preferred stock. Tier<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>2 capital consists of instruments disqualified from Tier<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>1 capital, including </div><div id="a8077" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:922px;">qualifying subordinated debt and a limited amount of loan loss reserves up<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to a maximum of 1.25% of risk-weighted assets, </div><div id="a8119" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:938px;">subject to certain eligibility criteria. The capital rules also define the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>risk-weights assigned to assets and off-balance sheet items to </div><div id="a8163" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:953px;">determine the risk-weighted asset components of the risk-based capital<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>rules, including, for example, certain &#8220;high volatility&#8221; </div><div id="a8199" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:968px;">commercial real estate, past due assets, structured securities, and equity<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>holdings. </div></div>

<div id="Page15" style="background-color:RGB(255, 255, 255);position:relative;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;overflow:hidden;border-style:solid;border-width:thin;border-color:RGB(198, 198, 198);page-break-after:always;width:816px;height:1056px;">
<div id="a8223" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:404px;top:1022px;">15 </div><div id="a8225" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:48px;">The leverage capital ratio, which serves as a minimum capital standard,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>is the ratio of Tier 1 capital to quarterly average<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>total </div><div id="a8269" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:64px;">consolidated assets net of goodwill, certain other intangible assets, and certain<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>required deduction items. The required minimum </div><div id="a8303" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:79px;">leverage ratio for all banks and bank holding companies is 4%. </div><div id="a8326" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:110px;">In addition, effective January 1, 2019, the capital rules required<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a capital conservation buffer of 2.5% above each of the minimum </div><div id="a8368" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:125px;">risk-based capital ratio requirements (CET1, Tier<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>1, and total capital), which is designed to absorb losses during periods of </div><div id="a8408" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:140px;">economic stress. These buffer requirements must be<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>met for a bank or bank holding company to be able to pay dividends, engage </div><div id="a8452" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:156px;">in share buybacks, or make discretionary bonus payments to executive<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>management without restriction. </div><div id="a8479" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:186px;">The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation Improvement Act (&#8220;FDICIA&#8221;),<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>among other things, requires the federal bank </div><div id="a8509" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:202px;">regulatory agencies to take &#8220;prompt corrective action&#8221; regarding depository<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>institutions that do not meet minimum capital </div><div id="a8541" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:217px;">requirements. FDICIA establishes five regulatory capital tiers: &#8220;well capitalized,&#8221;<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>&#8220;adequately capitalized,&#8221; &#8220;undercapitalized,&#8221; </div><div id="a8565" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:232px;">&#8220;significantly undercapitalized,&#8221; and &#8220;critically undercapitalized.&#8221; A depository<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>institution&#8217;s capital tier will depend<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>upon how its </div><div id="a8595" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:248px;">capital levels compare to various relevant capital measures and certain<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>other factors, as established by regulation. FDICIA </div><div id="a8629" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:263px;">generally prohibits a depository institution from making any capital distribution<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>(including payment of a dividend) or paying any </div><div id="a8665" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:278px;">management fee to its holding company if the depository institution would<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>thereafter be undercapitalized. The FDICIA imposes </div><div id="a8699" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:294px;">progressively more restrictive restraints on operations, management,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and capital distributions depending on the category in which </div><div id="a8731" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:309px;">an institution is classified. Undercapitalized depository institutions are<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>subject to restrictions on borrowing from the Federal </div><div id="a8763" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:324px;">Reserve System. In addition, undercapitalized depository institutions<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>may not accept brokered deposits absent a waiver from the </div><div id="a8797" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:340px;">FDIC, are subject to growth limitations, and are required to submit capital<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>restoration plans for regulatory approval. A depository </div><div id="a8835" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:355px;">institution's holding company must guarantee any required capital restoration<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>plan up to an amount equal to the lesser of 5% of </div><div id="a8877" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:370px;">the depository institution's assets at the time it becomes undercapitalized<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or the amount of the capital deficiency when the </div><div id="a8915" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:386px;">institution fails to comply with the plan. Federal banking agencies may not<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>accept a capital plan without determining, among </div><div id="a8953" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:401px;">other things, that the plan is based on realistic assumptions and is likely to<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>succeed in restoring the depository institution's capital. </div><div id="a8995" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:416px;">If a depository institution fails to submit an acceptable plan, it is treated as if it is significantly<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>undercapitalized. </div><div id="a9034" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:447px;">To be well-capitalized,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the Bank must maintain at least the following capital ratios: </div><div id="a9062" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:134px;top:463px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a9064" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:158px;top:463px;">6.5% CET1 to risk-weighted assets; </div><div id="a9076" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:134px;top:480px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a9078" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:158px;top:480px;">8.0% Tier 1 capital to risk-weighted assets; </div><div id="a9094" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:134px;top:496px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a9096" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:158px;top:496px;">10.0% Total capital to<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>risk-weighted assets; and </div><div id="a9112" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:134px;top:512px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a9114" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:158px;top:512px;">5.0% leverage ratio. </div><div id="a9121" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:543px;">The Federal Reserve has not yet revised the well-capitalized standard<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>for bank holding companies to reflect the higher capital </div><div id="a9161" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:558px;">requirements imposed under the current capital rules applicable to<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>banks. For purposes of the Federal Reserve&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Regulation </div><div id="a9195" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:724px;top:558px;">Y, </div><div id="a9197" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:574px;">including determining whether a bank holding company meets the requirements<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to be a financial holding company,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>bank holding </div><div id="a9233" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:589px;">companies, such as the Company,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>must maintain a Tier 1 risk-based capital ratio of 6.0%<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or greater and a total risk-based capital </div><div id="a9281" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:604px;">ratio of 10.0% or greater to be well-capitalized. Also, the Federal Reserve<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>may require bank holding companies, including the </div><div id="a9321" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:619px;">Company, to maintain<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>capital ratios substantially in excess of mandated minimum levels depending<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>upon general economic </div><div id="a9353" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:635px;">conditions and a bank holding company&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>particular condition, risk profile, and growth plans. </div><div id="a9380" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:666px;">Failure to be well-capitalized or to meet minimum capital requirements<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>could result in certain mandatory and possible additional </div><div id="a9418" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:681px;">discretionary actions by regulators that, if undertaken, could have an adverse<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>material effect on our operations or financial </div><div id="a9454" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:696px;">condition. Failure to meet minimum capital requirements could also result<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in restrictions on the Company&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or the Bank&#8217;s ability </div><div id="a9492" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:711px;">to pay dividends or otherwise distribute capital or to receive regulatory<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>approval of applications or other restrictions on its growth. </div><div id="a9533" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:742px;">In 2025, the Company&#8217;s and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the Bank&#8217;s regulatory capital ratios were above<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the applicable well-capitalized standards and met the </div><div id="a9573" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>all applicable well-</div><div id="a9612" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:773px;">capitalized regulatory capital requirements and the capital conservation<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>buffer in 2026. </div><div id="a9637" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:804px;">Payment of Dividends </div><div id="a9644" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:834px;">We </div><div id="a9646" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:84px;top:834px;">are a legal entity separate and distinct from the Bank and our other subsidiaries.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Under the laws of the State of Florida, we, as </div><div id="a9694" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:850px;">a business corporation, may declare and pay dividends in cash or property<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>unless the payment or declaration would be contrary to </div><div total </div><div id="a9830" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:896px;">liabilities. In addition, we are also subject to federal regulatory capital requirements<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>that effectively limit the amount of cash </div><div id="a9868" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:911px;">dividends that we may pay. </div></div>

<div id="Page16" style="background-color:RGB(255, 255, 255);position:relative;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;overflow:hidden;border-style:solid;border-width:thin;border-color:RGB(198, 198, 198);page-break-after:always;width:816px;height:1056px;">
<div id="a9880" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:404px;top:1022px;">16 </div><div id="a9882" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:48px;">Under a Federal Reserve policy adopted in 2009, the board of directors<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of a bank holding company must consider different factors </div><div id="a9924" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:64px;">to ensure that its dividend level is prudent relative to maintaining a strong<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>financial position and is not based on overly optimistic </div><div id="a9968" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:79px;">earnings scenarios, such as potential events that could affect its ability<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to pay, while still maintaining<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a strong financial position. </div><div id="a10008" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:94px;">As a general matter, the Federal Reserve has indicated<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>that the board of directors of a bank holding company should consult with </div><div id="a10052" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:110px;">the Federal Reserve and eliminate, defer,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or significantly reduce the bank holding company&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>dividends if: </div><div id="a10082" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:86px;top:126px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a10084" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:126px;">its net income available to shareholders for the past four quarters, net<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of dividends previously paid during that period, is </div><div id="a10124" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:141px;">not sufficient to fully fund the dividends; </div><div id="a10138" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:86px;top:158px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a10140" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:158px;">its prospective rate of earnings retention is not consistent with its capital needs and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>overall current and prospective </div><div id="a10176" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:173px;">financial condition; or </div><div id="a10182" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:86px;top:189px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a10184" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:189px;">it will not meet, or is in danger of not meeting, its minimum regulatory capital<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>adequacy ratios. </div><div id="a10219" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:220px;">The primary sources of funds for our payment of dividends to our shareholders<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>are cash on hand and dividends from the Bank and </div><div id="a10265" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:235px;">our non-bank subsidiaries. The Bank is subject to legal limitations on<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the frequency and amount of dividends that can be paid to </div><div id="a10311" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:250px;">the Company. The<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Federal Reserve may restrict the ability of the Bank to pay dividends if such payments would<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>constitute an </div><div id="a10353" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:266px;">unsafe or unsound banking practice.<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a10365" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:297px;">In addition, Florida law and Federal regulation place restrictions on the declaration<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of dividends from state-chartered banks to </div><div id="a10403" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:312px;">their holding companies. Under the Florida Financial Institutions Code,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the board of directors of a state-chartered bank, after it </div><div id="a10443" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:327px;">charges off bad debts, depreciation and other<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>worthless assets, if any, and makes provisions<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>for reasonably anticipated future </div><div id="a10479" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:343px;">losses on loans and other assets, may quarterly,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>semi-annually or annually declare a dividend of up to the aggregate net profits of </div><div id="a10525" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:358px;">that period combined with the bank&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>retained net profits for the preceding two years. In addition, with the approval of the Florida </div><div id="a10569" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:373px;">OFR and Federal Reserve, the bank&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>board of directors may declare a dividend from retained net profits which<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>accrued prior to </div><div id="a10611" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:389px;">the preceding two years. Before declaring such dividends, 20% of the net profits for<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the preceding period as is covered by the </div><div id="a10655" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:404px;">dividend must be transferred to the surplus fund of the bank until this fund becomes<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>equal to the amount of the bank&#8217;s common </div><div id="a10701" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:419px;">stock then issued and outstanding. However,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a Florida state-chartered bank may not declare any dividend if (i) its net income </div><div id="a10743" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:435px;">(loss) from the current year combined with the retained net income (loss) for<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the preceding two years aggregates a loss or (ii) the </div><div id="a10789" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:450px;">payment of such dividend would cause the capital account of the bank<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to fall below the minimum amount required by law, </div><div id="a10831" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:465px;">regulation, order or any written agreement with the Florida OFR or a federal<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>regulatory agency. Under<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Federal Reserve </div><div id="a10867" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:481px;">regulations, a state member bank may,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>without the prior approval of the Federal Reserve, pay a dividend in an amount that, when </div><div id="a10911" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:496px;">taken together with all dividends declared during the calendar year,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>does not exceed the sum of the bank&#8217;s net<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>income during the </div><div id="a10955" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:511px;">current calendar year and the retained net income of the prior two calendar years.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>The Federal Reserve may approve greater </div><div id="a10995" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:527px;">amounts. </div><div id="a10998" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:557px;">In addition, we and the Bank are subject to various general regulatory policies<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and requirements relating to the payment of </div><div id="a11038" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:573px;">dividends, including requirements to maintain adequate capital above<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>regulatory minimums. The Federal Reserve has indicated </div><div id="a11068" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:588px;">that paying dividends that deplete a bank&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>capital base to an inadequate level would be an unsafe and unsound banking<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>practice. </div><div id="a11110" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:603px;">The Federal Reserve has indicated that depository institutions and their<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>holding companies should generally pay dividends only </div><div id="a11144" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:619px;">out of current operating earnings. </div><div id="a11155" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:649px;">Safe and Sound Banking Practices </div><div id="a11166" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:680px;">Bank holding companies and their nonbanking subsidiaries are prohibited<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>from engaging in activities that represent unsafe and </div><div id="a11200" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:695px;">unsound banking practices or that constitute a violation of law or regulations.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Under certain conditions the Federal Reserve may </div><div id="a11238" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:711px;">conclude that some actions of a bank holding company,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>such as a payment of a cash dividend, would constitute an unsafe and </div><div id="a11282" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:726px;">unsound banking practice. The Federal Reserve also has the authority<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to regulate the debt of bank holding companies, including </div><div id="a11320" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:741px;">the authority to impose interest rate ceilings and reserve requirements on<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>such debt. The Federal Reserve may also require a bank </div><div id="a11362" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:757px;">holding company to file written notice and obtain its approval prior to purchasing<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or redeeming its equity securities, unless certain </div><div id="a11402" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:772px;">conditions are met.<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a11410" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:803px;">Capital City Bank </div><div id="a11417" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:833px;">Capital City Bank is a state-chartered commercial banking institution that is chartered<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>by and headquartered in the State of Florida </div><div id="a11420" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:849px;">and is subject to supervision and regulation by the Florida OFR. The Florida OFR supervises and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>regulates all areas of our </div><div id="a11421" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:864px;">operations including, without limitation, the making of loans, the issuance of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>securities, the conduct of our corporate affairs, the </div><div id="a11423" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:879px;">satisfaction of capital adequacy requirements, the payment of dividends,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and the establishment or closing of banking centers. We </div><div id="a11426" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:895px;">are also a member bank of the Federal Reserve System, which makes our operations<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>subject to broad federal regulation and </div><div id="a11427" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:910px;">oversight by the Federal Reserve. In addition, our deposit accounts are insured<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>by the FDIC up to the maximum extent permitted </div><div id="a11429" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:925px;">by law, and the FDIC has certain<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>supervisory enforcement powers over us.<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div></div></div>
