<div id="Page17" style="background-color:RGB(255, 255, 255);position:relative;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;overflow:hidden;border-style:solid;border-width:thin;border-color:RGB(198, 198, 198);page-break-after:always;width:816px;height:1056px;">
<div id="a11433" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:404px;top:1022px;">17 </div><div id="a11435" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:48px;">As a Florida state-chartered bank, we are empowered by statute, subject to<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the limitations contained in those statutes, to take and </div><div id="a11438" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:64px;">pay interest on savings and time deposits, to accept demand deposits, to<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>make loans on residential and other real estate, to make </div><div id="a11440" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:79px;">consumer and commercial loans, to invest (with certain limitations) in equity securities<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and in debt obligations of banks and </div><div id="a11442" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:94px;">corporations and to provide various other banking services for the benefit<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of our clients. Various<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>consumer laws and regulations </div><div id="a11444" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:110px;">also affect our operations, including state usury laws, laws relating to<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>fiduciaries, consumer credit and equal credit opportunity </div><div id="a11446" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:125px;">laws, and fair credit reporting. In addition, FDICIA prohibits insured state-chartered<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>institutions from conducting activities as </div><div id="a11449" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:140px;">principal that are not permitted for national banks. A bank, however,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>may engage in certain otherwise prohibited activity if it </div><div id="a11451" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:156px;">meets its minimum capital requirements and the FDIC determines that the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>activity does not present a significant risk to the DIF. </div><div id="a11455" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:186px;">Safety and Soundness Standards / Risk Management </div><div id="a11470" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:217px;">The Federal Deposit Insurance Act requires the federal bank regulatory<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>agencies to prescribe, by regulation or guideline, </div><div id="a11504" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:232px;">operational and managerial standards for all insured depository institutions<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>relating to: (i) internal controls; (ii) information </div><div id="a11536" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:248px;">systems and audit systems; (iii) loan documentation; (iv) credit underwriting;<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>(v) interest rate risk exposure; and (vi) asset quality. </div><div id="a11574" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:263px;">The federal banking agencies have adopted regulations and Interagency<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Guidelines Establishing Standards for Safety and </div><div id="a11604" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:278px;">Soundness to implement these required standards. These guidelines set forth<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the safety and soundness standards used to identify </div><div id="a11640" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:294px;">and address problems at insured depository institutions before capital<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>becomes impaired. Under the regulations, if a regulator </div><div id="a11674" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:309px;">determines that a bank fails to meet any standards prescribed by<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the guidelines, the regulator may require the bank to submit an </div><div id="a11718" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:324px;">acceptable plan to achieve compliance, consistent with deadlines for<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the submission and review of such safety and soundness </div><div id="a11754" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:340px;">compliance plans. </div><div id="a11759" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:370px;">The bank regulatory agencies have increasingly emphasized the importance<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of sound risk management processes and strong </div><div id="a11760" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:386px;">internal controls when evaluating the activities of the financial institutions they<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>supervise. Properly managing risks has been </div><div id="a11762" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:401px;">identified as critical to the conduct of safe and sound banking activities and has<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>become even more important as new </div><div id="a11763" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:416px;">technologies, product innovation and the size and speed of financial transactions have<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>changed the nature of banking markets. The </div><div id="a11766" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:432px;">agencies have identified a spectrum of risks facing a banking institution including,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>but not limited to, credit, market, liquidity, </div><div id="a11768" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:447px;">operational, legal and reputational risk. A particular area of focus for regulators<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>has been operational risk, which arises from the </div><div id="a11770" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:462px;">potential that inadequate information systems, operational problems,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>breaches in internal controls, fraud or unforeseen </div><div id="a11771" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:478px;">catastrophes will result in unexpected losses. New products and services, third<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>party risk management and cybersecurity are </div><div id="a11772" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:493px;">critical sources of operational risk that financial institutions are expected<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to address in the current environment. The Bank is </div><div id="a11775" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:508px;">expected to have active board and senior management oversight; adequate<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>policies, procedures and limits; adequate risk </div><div id="a11776" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:524px;">measurement, monitoring and management information systems; and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>comprehensive internal controls. </div><div id="a11779" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:554px;">Insurance of Accounts and Other Assessments<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a11793" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:585px;">The Bank&#8217;s deposits are insured<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>by the FDIC&#8217;s DIF up to the limits under<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>applicable law, which currently<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>are set at $250,000 per </div><div id="a11795" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:600px;">depositor, per insured bank, for each account<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>ownership category. The Bank<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>is subject to FDIC assessments for its deposit </div><div id="a11796" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:616px;">insurance. The FDIC calculates quarterly deposit insurance assessments based<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>on an institution&#8217;s average<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>total consolidated assets </div><div id="a11798" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:631px;">less its average tangible equity and applies one of four risk categories determined<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>by reference to its capital levels, supervisory </div><div id="a11800" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:646px;">ratings, and certain other factors. The assessment rate schedule can change<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>from time to time, at the discretion of the FDIC, </div><div id="a11802" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:662px;">subject to certain limits.<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a11805" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:692px;">As of June 30, 2020, the DIF reserve ratio fell to 1.30%, below the statutory<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>minimum of 1.35%. The FDIC, as required under the </div><div id="a11807" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:708px;">Federal Deposit Insurance Act, established a plan on September 15, 2020<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to restore the DIF reserve ratio to meet or exceed the </div><div id="a11809" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:723px;">statutory minimum of 1.35% within eight years. On October 18, 2022,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the FDIC adopted an amended restoration plan to increase </div><div id="a11810" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:738px;">the likelihood that the reserve ratio would be restored to at least 1.35% by September<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>30, 2028. The FDIC's amended restoration </div><div id="a11812" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:754px;">plan increased the initial base deposit insurance assessment rate schedules<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>uniformly by 2 bps, beginning with the first quarterly </div><div id="a11814" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:769px;">assessment period of 2023. The FDIC could further increase the deposit<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>insurance assessments for certain insured depository </div><div id="a11815" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:784px;">institutions, including the Bank, if the DIF reserve ratio is not restored as projected.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a11818" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:815px;">In November 2023, the FDIC approved a final rule to implement a special assessment to<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>recover the loss to the DIF associated </div><div id="a11819" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:830px;">with several bank failures that occurred during the first half of 2023. The assessment base<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>for the special assessment is equal to a </div><div id="a11821" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:846px;">bank's uninsured deposits reported as of December 31, 2022, adjusted<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to exclude the first $5 billion, to be collected at an annual </div><div id="a11823" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:861px;">rate of approximately 13.4 bps for an anticipated total of eight quarterly<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>assessment periods, beginning with the first quarterly </div><div id="a11825" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:876px;">assessment period of 2024. The final rule does not apply to any banking organization<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>with less than $5 billion in total </div><div id="a11826" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:892px;">consolidated assets and therefore the special assessment did not directly<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>impact the Bank. </div></div>

<div id="a11830" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:404px;top:1022px;">18 </div><div id="a11832" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:48px;">Insurance of deposits may be terminated by the FDIC upon a finding that the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>institution has engaged in unsafe and unsound </div><div id="a11833" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:64px;">practices, is in an unsafe or unsound condition to continue operations, or has violated<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>any applicable law, regulation,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>rule, order, </div><div id="a11836" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:79px;">or condition imposed by a bank&#8217;s federal<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>regulatory agency. In addition,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the Federal Deposit Insurance Act provides that, in the </div><div id="a11838" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:94px;">event of the liquidation or other resolution of an insured depository institution,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the claims of depositors of the institution, </div><div id="a11840" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:110px;">including the claims of the FDIC as subrogee of insured depositors, and certain<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>claims for administrative expenses of the FDIC as </div><div id="a11842" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:125px;">a receiver, will have priority over other general<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>unsecured claims against the institution, including those of the parent bank </div><div id="a11844" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:140px;">holding company. </div><div id="a11847" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:171px;">Transactions with Affiliates and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Insiders </div><div id="a11858" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:202px;">The Bank is subject to restrictions on extensions of credit and certain<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>other transactions between the Bank and the Company or </div><div id="a11900" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:217px;">any nonbank affiliate. Generally,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>these covered transactions with either the Company or any affiliate<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>are limited to 10% of the </div><div id="a11940" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:232px;">Bank&#8217;s capital and surplus, and all such<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>transactions between the Bank and the Company and all of its nonbank affiliates </div><div id="a11980" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:248px;">combined are limited to 20% of the Bank&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>capital and surplus. Loans and other extensions of credit from the Bank to the </div><div id="a12024" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:263px;">Company or any affiliate generally are required<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to be secured by eligible collateral in specified amounts. In addition, any </div><div id="a12062" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:278px;">transaction between the Bank and the Company or any affiliate are<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>required to be on an arm&#8217;s length<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>basis. Federal banking laws </div><div id="a12106" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:294px;">also place similar restrictions on certain extensions of credit by insured banks,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>such as the Bank, to their directors, executive </div><div id="a12146" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:309px;">officers, and principal shareholders. </div><div id="a12155" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:340px;">Anti-Tying Restrictions</div><div id="a12162" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:370px;">In general, a bank may not extend credit, lease, sell property,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or furnish any services or fix or vary the consideration for them on </div><div id="a12210" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:386px;">the condition that (i) the client obtain or provide some additional credit, property,<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>or services from or to the bank or bank holding </div><div id="a12256" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:401px;">company or their subsidiaries or (ii) the client not obtain some other credit, property,<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>or services from a competitor, except to the </div><div id="a12300" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:416px;">extent reasonable conditions are imposed to assure the soundness of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the credit extended. A bank may,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>however, offer combined-</div><div id="a12338" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:432px;">balance products and may otherwise offer more favorable<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>terms if a client obtains two or more traditional bank products. The law </div><div id="a12380" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:447px;">also expressly permits banks to engage in other forms of tying and authorizes<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the Federal Reserve Board to grant additional </div><div id="a12420" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:462px;">exceptions by regulation or order.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Also, certain foreign transactions are exempt from the general rule. </div><div id="a12451" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:493px;">Community Reinvestment Act </div><div id="a12458" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:524px;">The Bank is subject to the provisions of the CRA, which imposes a continuing and affirmative<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>obligation, consistent with safe and </div><div id="a12461" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:539px;">sound operation, to help meet the credit needs of entire communities where the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>bank accepts deposits, including low- and </div><div id="a12465" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:554px;">moderate-income neighborhoods. The Federal Reserve&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>assessment of the Bank&#8217;s CRA record<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>is made available to the public. </div><div id="a12468" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:570px;">CRA agreements with private parties must be disclosed and annual<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>CRA reports must be made to the Federal Reserve. A bank </div><div id="a12469" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:585px;">holding company will not be permitted to become or remain a financial<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>holding company and no new activities authorized under </div><div id="a12470" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:600px;">GLB may be commenced by a holding company or by a bank financial subsidiary<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>if any of its bank subsidiaries received less than </div><div id="a12472" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:616px;">a &#8220;satisfactory&#8221; CRA rating in its latest CRA examination. Federal CRA regulations<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>require, among other things, that evidence of </div><div id="a12475" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:631px;">discrimination against applicants on a prohibited basis and illegal or abusive lending<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>practices be considered in the CRA </div><div id="a12476" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:646px;">evaluation. The Bank has a rating of &#8220;Satisfactory&#8221; in its most recent CRA evaluation. </div><div id="a12479" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:677px;">In 2023 the Federal Reserve, OCC, and FDIC issued a final rule to modernize their<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>respective CRA regulations. The revised rules </div><div id="a12481" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:692px;">would substantially alter the methodology for assessing compliance with<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the CRA, with material aspects taking effect January<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>1, </div><div id="a12483" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:708px;">2026 and revised data reporting requirements taking effect<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>January 1, 2027. The revised CRA regulations have been subject to an </div><div id="a12485" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:723px;">injunction since March 29, 2024. On July 16, 2025, the Federal Reserve, OCC, and FDIC<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>issued a joint proposal to rescind the </div><div id="a12486" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:738px;">2023 modernization rule. The agencies continue to apply the CRA rules as they existed<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>before the 2023 modernization, </div><div id="a12487" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:754px;">considering the injunction and pending finalization of the recission of the modernization<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>rule. </div><div id="a12490" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:784px;">Commercial Real Estate Concentration Guidelines<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a12502" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:815px;">The federal banking regulators have implemented guidelines to address<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>increased concentrations in commercial real estate loans. </div><div id="a12534" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:830px;">These guidelines describe the criteria regulatory agencies will use as indicators<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to identify institutions potentially exposed to </div><div id="a12568" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:846px;">commercial real estate concentration risk. An institution that has (i) experienced<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>rapid growth in commercial real estate lending, </div><div id="a12604" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:861px;">(ii) notable exposure to a specific type of<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>commercial real estate, (iii) total reported loans for construction, land development,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and </div><div id="a12644" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:876px;">other land representing 100% or more of total risk-based capital, or (iv)<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>total commercial real estate (including construction) loans </div><div id="a12684" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:892px;">representing 300% or more of total risk-based capital and the outstanding<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>balance of the institutions commercial real estate </div><div id="a12722" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:907px;">portfolio has increased by 50% or more in the prior 36 months, may be identified<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>for further supervisory analysis of a potential </div><div id="a12766" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:922px;">concentration risk.<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div></div></div>
</div>

<div id="Page19" style="background-color:RGB(255, 255, 255);position:relative;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;overflow:hidden;border-style:solid;border-width:thin;border-color:RGB(198, 198, 198);page-break-after:always;width:816px;height:1056px;">
<div id="a12774" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:404px;top:1022px;">19 </div><div id="a12776" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:48px;">At December 31, 2025, CCB&#8217;s ratio<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of construction, land development and other land loans to total tier 1 risk-based<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>capital was </div><div id="a12822" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:64px;">49%, its ratio of commercial real estate loans to total tier 1 risk-based capital was 119%<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and, therefore, CCB was under the 100% </div><div id="a12875" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:79px;">and 300% thresholds, respectively,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>set forth in clauses (iii) and (iv) above.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>As a result, we are not deemed to have a concentration </div><div id="a12921" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:94px;">in commercial real estate lending under applicable regulatory guidelines. </div><div id="a12940" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:125px;">Interstate Banking and Branching </div><div id="a12949" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:156px;">The Dodd-Frank Act relaxed interstate branching restrictions by modifying<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the federal statute governing de novo interstate </div><div id="a12983" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:171px;">branching by state member banks. Consequently,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a state member bank may open its initial branch in a state outside of the bank&#8217;s </div><div id="a13027" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:186px;">home state by way of an interstate bank branch, so long as a bank chartered under<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the laws of that state would be permitted to </div><div id="a13077" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:202px;">open a branch at that location.<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a13092" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:232px;">Anti-money Laundering </div><div id="a13099" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:263px;">A continued focus of governmental policy relating to financial institutions in recent<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>years has been combating money laundering </div><div id="a13135" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:278px;">and terrorist financing. The USA PATRIOT<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Act broadened the application of anti-money laundering<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>regulations to apply to </div><div id="a13171" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:294px;">additional types of financial institutions such as broker-dealers, investment advisors,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and insurance companies, and strengthened </div><div id="a13203" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:309px;">the ability of the U.S. government to help prevent, detect, and prosecute<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>international money laundering and the financing of </div><div id="a13241" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:324px;">terrorism. The principal provisions of Title<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>III of the USA PATRIOT<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>Act require that regulated financial institutions, including </div><div id="a13277" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:340px;">state member banks: (i) establish an anti-money laundering program<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>that includes training and audit components; (ii) comply with </div><div id="a13315" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:355px;">regulations regarding the verification of the identity of any person seeking<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to open an account; (iii) take additional required </div><div id="a13353" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:370px;">precautions with non-U.S. owned accounts; and (iv) perform certain<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>verification and certification of money laundering risk for </div><div id="a13389" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:386px;">their foreign correspondent banking relationships. Failure of a<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>financial institution to comply with the USA PATRIOT<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Act&#8217;s </div><div id="a13423" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:401px;">requirements could have serious legal and reputational consequences<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>for the institution. The Bank has augmented its systems and </div><div id="a13459" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:416px;">procedures to meet the requirements of these regulations and will continue<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to revise and update its policies, procedures, and </div><div id="a13497" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:432px;">controls to reflect changes required by law. </div><div id="a13512" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:462px;">FinCEN has adopted rules that require financial institutions to obtain beneficial<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>ownership information with respect to legal </div><div id="a13546" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:478px;">entities with which such institutions conduct business, subject to certain exclusions<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and exemptions. Bank regulators are focusing </div><div id="a13580" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:493px;">their examinations on anti-money laundering compliance, and we continue<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to monitor and augment, where necessary,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>our anti-</div><div id="a13616" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:508px;">money laundering compliance programs. Banking regulators will consider<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>compliance with the USA PATRIOT<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Act&#8217;s money </div><div id="a13646" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:524px;">laundering provisions in acting upon merger and acquisition<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>proposals. Bank regulators routinely examine institutions for </div><div id="a13676" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:539px;">compliance with these obligations and have been active in imposing<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>cease and desist and other regulatory orders and civil money </div><div id="a13716" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:554px;">penalties against institutions found to be violating these obligations.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Sanctions for violations of the USA PATRIOT<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Act can be </div><div id="a13754" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:570px;">imposed in an amount equal to twice the sum involved in the violating transaction<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>up to $1 million. The Anti-Money Laundering </div><div id="a13798" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:585px;">Act (&#8220;AMLA&#8221;), which amends the BSA, was enacted in early 2021. The AMLA<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>is intended to be a comprehensive reform and </div><div id="a13840" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:600px;">modernization of U.S. bank secrecy and anti-money laundering<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>laws. In particular, it codifies a risk-based approach<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to anti-money </div><div id="a13882" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:616px;">laundering compliance for financial institutions, requires the U.S. Department<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of the Treasury to promulgate priorities for anti-</div><div id="a13916" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:631px;">money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism policy,<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>requires the development of standards for testing technology </div><div id="a13950" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:646px;">and internal processes for BSA compliance, expands enforcement<div style="display:inline-block;width:1px">&#160;</div>-<div style="display:inline-block;width:3px">&#160;</div>and investigation-related authority (including increasing </div><div id="a13979" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:662px;">available sanctions for certain BSA violations), and expands BSA whistleblower<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>incentives and protections. </div><div id="a14006" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:692px;">Many AMLA provisions require additional rulemakings, reports,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and other measures, and the impact of the AMLA will depend </div><div id="a14042" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:708px;">on, among other things, rulemaking and implementation<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>guidance. In June 2021, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, a </div><div id="a14076" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:723px;">bureau of the U.S. Department of the Treasury,<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>issued the priorities for anti-money laundering and countering the financing of </div><div id="a14116" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:738px;">terrorism policy required under the AMLA. The priorities include corruption,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>cybercrime, terrorist financing, fraud, transnational </div><div id="a14146" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:754px;">crime, drug trafficking, human trafficking<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and proliferation financing. </div><div id="a14163" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:784px;">Economic Sanctions </div><div id="a14166" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:815px;">OFAC is responsible<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>for helping to ensure that U.S. entities do not engage in transactions with certain<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>prohibited parties, as </div><div id="a14168" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:830px;">defined by various executive orders and acts of Congress. OFAC<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>publishes, and routinely updates, lists of names of persons and </div><div id="a14170" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:846px;">organizations suspected of aiding, harboring, or engaging<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in terrorist acts, including the Specially Designated Nationals and </div><div id="a14172" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:861px;">Blocked Persons List. If we find a name on any transaction, account, or wire transfer<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>that is on an OFAC list, we must undertake </div><div id="a14174" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:876px;">certain specified activities, which could include blocking or freezing<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the account or transaction requested, and we must notify the </div><div id="a14176" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:892px;">appropriate authorities. </div></div>

<div id="a14180" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:404px;top:1022px;">20 </div><div id="a14182" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:48px;">Privacy, Credit Reporting, and Data Security </div><div id="a14187" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:79px;">The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (&#8220;GLB&#8221;) generally prohibits disclosure<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of non-public consumer information to non-affiliated third </div><div id="a14223" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:94px;">parties unless the consumer has been given the opportunity to object and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>has not objected to such disclosure. Financial institutions </div><div id="a14263" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:110px;">are further required to disclose their privacy policies to clients annually.<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>Financial institutions, however, will be required<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to </div><div id="a14299" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:125px;">comply with state law if it is more protective of consumer privacy than the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>GLB. The GLB also directed federal regulators to </div><div id="a14343" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:140px;">prescribe standards for the security of consumer information. The<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Bank is subject to such standards, as well as standards for </div><div id="a14383" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:156px;">notifying clients in the event of a security breach. The Bank utilizes credit bureau<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>data in underwriting activities. Use of such data </div><div id="a14427" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:171px;">is regulated under the Fair Credit Reporting Act and Regulation V on<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a uniform, nationwide basis, including credit reporting, </div><div id="a14465" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:186px;">prescreening, and sharing of information between affiliates<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and the use of credit data. The Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions </div><div id="a14503" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:202px;">Act, which amended the Fair Credit Reporting Act, permits states to enact identity<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>theft laws that are not inconsistent with the </div><div id="a14545" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:217px;">conduct required by the provisions of that Act. Clients must be notified<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>when unauthorized disclosure involves sensitive client </div><div id="a14581" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:232px;">information that may be misused. On November 18, 2021, the federal<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>banking agencies issued a new rule effective in 2022 that </div><div id="a14623" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:248px;">requires banks to notify their primary federal regulator within 36<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>hours of a &#8220;computer-security incident&#8221; that rises to the level of </div><div id="a14667" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:263px;">a &#8220;notification incident.&#8221; In addition, effective in December 2023,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the SEC issued a new rule that generally requires SEC </div><div id="a14705" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:278px;">registrants to disclose on Form 8-K certain information about a material<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>cybersecurity incident within four business days of </div><div id="a14743" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:294px;">determining it is material, with periodic updates as to the status of the incident in<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>subsequent filings, as necessary.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>The SEC rule </div><div id="a14787" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:309px;">also requires registrants to disclose certain information concerning<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>cybersecurity risk management, strategy and governance on </div><div id="a14817" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:324px;">Form 10-K. </div><div id="a14824" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:355px;">The federal banking regulators regularly issue guidance regarding<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>cybersecurity intended to enhance cyber risk management </div><div id="a14825" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:370px;">standards among financial institutions. As a result, financial institutions, like the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Company and the Bank, are expected to establish </div><div id="a14827" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:386px;">multiple lines of defense and to ensure their risk management processes address<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the risk posed by potential threats to the </div><div id="a14828" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:401px;">institution. A financial institution&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>management is expected to maintain sufficient processes to effectively<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>respond and recover </div><div id="a14830" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:416px;">the institution&#8217;s operations after<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a cyber-attack. A financial institution is also expected to develop<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>appropriate processes to enable </div><div id="a14833" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:432px;">recovery of data and business operations if a critical service provider<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of the institution falls victim to this type of cyber-attack. In </div><div id="a14836" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:447px;">addition, effective in December 2023, the SEC enhanced and standardized<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the disclosure obligations related to a registrant's </div><div id="a14837" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:462px;">cybersecurity risk management, strategy,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and governance. Our information security protocols are designed in part to adhere to<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the </div><div id="a14840" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:478px;">requirements of bank regulatory guidance and these enhanced SEC disclosure requirements.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>See "Part I - Item 1C. Cybersecurity" </div><div id="a14844" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:493px;">of this Report for additional information on cybersecurity. </div><div id="a14847" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:524px;">State regulators have also been increasingly active in implementing privacy<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and cybersecurity standards and regulations. </div><div id="a14848" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:539px;">Recently, several states have<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>adopted regulations requiring certain financial institutions to implement<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>cybersecurity programs and </div><div id="a14850" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:554px;">providing detailed requirements with respect to these programs, including data<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>encryption requirements. Many states have also </div><div id="a14852" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:570px;">recently implemented or modified their data breach notification and data<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>privacy requirements. We<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>expect this trend of state-level </div><div id="a14855" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:585px;">activity in those areas to continue and are continually monitoring developments in<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the states in which our clients are located. </div><div id="a14859" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:616px;">See Item 1A. Risk Factors for a further discussion of risks related to cybersecurity<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and Item 1C. Cybersecurity for a further </div><div id="a14861" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:631px;">discussion of risk management strategies and governance processes related to<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>cybersecurity. </div></div>

<div id="Page21" style="background-color:RGB(255, 255, 255);position:relative;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;overflow:hidden;border-style:solid;border-width:thin;border-color:RGB(198, 198, 198);page-break-after:always;width:816px;height:1056px;">
<div id="a14865" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:404px;top:1022px;">21 </div><div id="a14867" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:48px;">Consumer Laws and Regulations </div><div id="a14876" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:79px;">Activities of the Bank are subject to a variety of statutes and regulations designed<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to protect consumers. These laws and </div><div id="a14877" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:94px;">regulations include, among numerous other things, provisions that: </div><div id="a14880" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:86px;top:126px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a14882" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:126px;">limit the interest and other charges collected or contracted for by<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the Bank, including rules respecting the terms of credit </div><div id="a14883" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:141px;">cards and of debit card overdrafts; </div><div id="a14885" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:86px;top:158px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a14887" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:158px;">govern the Bank&#8217;s disclosures of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>credit terms to consumer borrowers; </div><div id="a14889" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:86px;top:174px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a14891" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:174px;">require the Bank to provide information to enable the public and public officials<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to determine whether it is fulfilling its </div><div id="a14892" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:189px;">obligation to help meet the housing needs of the communities it serves; </div><div id="a14894" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:86px;top:206px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a14896" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:206px;">prohibit the Bank from discriminating on the basis of race, creed, or other prohibited<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>factors when it makes decisions to </div><div id="a14897" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:221px;">extend credit; </div><div id="a14899" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:86px;top:237px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a14901" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:237px;">govern the manner in which the Bank may collect consumer debts; and </div><div id="a14903" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:86px;top:253px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a14905" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:253px;">prohibit unfair, deceptive, or abusive<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>acts or practices in the provision of consumer financial products and services. </div><div id="a14908" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:284px;">The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (&#8220;CFPB&#8221;) adopted a rule<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>that implements the ability-to-repay and qualified mortgage </div><div id="a14913" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:299px;">provisions of the Dodd-Frank Act (the &#8220;ATR/QM<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>rule&#8221;), which requires lenders to consider,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>among other things, income, </div><div id="a14916" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:315px;">employment status, assets, payment amounts, and credit history before<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>approving a mortgage, and provides a compliance &#8220;safe </div><div id="a14917" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:330px;">harbor&#8221; for lenders that issue certain &#8220;qualified mortgages.&#8221; The ATR/QM<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>rule defines a &#8220;qualified mortgage&#8221; to have certain </div><div id="a14918" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:345px;">specified characteristics and generally prohibits loans with negative amortization,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>interest-only payments, balloon payments, or </div><div id="a14921" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:361px;">terms exceeding 30 years from being qualified mortgages. The<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>rule also establishes general underwriting criteria for qualified </div><div id="a14923" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:376px;">mortgages, including that monthly payments be calculated based on the highest<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>payment that will apply in the first five years of </div><div id="a14926" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:391px;">the loan and that the borrower have a total debt-to-income ratio that is less than or<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>equal to 43%. While &#8220;qualified mortgages&#8221; will </div><div id="a14931" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:407px;">generally be afforded safe harbor status, a rebuttable presumption<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of compliance with the ability-to-repay requirements will attach </div><div id="a14936" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:422px;">to &#8220;qualified mortgages&#8221; that are &#8220;higher priced mortgages&#8221; (which are generally<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>subprime loans). In addition, the securitizer of </div><div id="a14938" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:437px;">asset-backed securities must retain not less than 5% of the credit risk of the assets collateralizing<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the asset-backed securities, </div><div id="a14943" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:453px;">unless subject to an exemption for asset-backed securities that are collateralized<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>exclusively by residential mortgages that qualify </div><div id="a14946" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:468px;">as &#8220;qualified residential mortgages.&#8221; </div><div id="a14949" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:499px;">The CFPB has also issued rules to implement requirements of the Dodd-Frank<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Act pertaining to mortgage loan origination </div><div id="a14952" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:514px;">(including with respect to loan originator compensation and loan originator qualifications)<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>as well as integrated mortgage </div><div id="a14953" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:529px;">disclosure rules. In addition, the CFPB has issued rules that require servicers<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to comply with certain standards and practices with </div><div id="a14955" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:545px;">regard to error correction; information disclosure; force-placement<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of insurance; information management policies and </div><div id="a14958" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:560px;">procedures; requiring information about mortgage loss mitigation options be<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>provided to delinquent borrowers; providing </div><div id="a14959" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:575px;">delinquent borrowers access to servicer personnel with continuity of contact<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>about the borrower&#8217;s mortgage loan account; and </div><div id="a14960" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:591px;">evaluating borrowers&#8217; applications for available loss mitigation options. These<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>rules also address initial rate adjustment notices for </div><div id="a14962" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:606px;">adjustable-rate mortgages, periodic statements for residential mortgage<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>loans, and prompt crediting of mortgage payments and </div><div id="a14965" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:621px;">response to requests for payoff amounts. </div><div id="a14968" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:652px;">Future Legislative Developments </div><div id="a14975" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:683px;">Various<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>bills are from time to time introduced in the U.S. Congress and the Florida legislature.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>This legislation may change </div><div id="a14976" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:698px;">banking and tax statutes and the environment in which our banking subsidiary<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and we operate in substantial and unpredictable </div><div id="a14977" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:713px;">ways. We cannot<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>determine the ultimate effect that potential legislation, if enacted, or<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>implementing regulations with respect </div><div id="a14979" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:729px;">thereto, would have upon our financial condition or results of operations or<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>that of our banking subsidiary. </div><div id="a14982" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:759px;">Effect of Governmental Monetary Policies </div><div id="a14993" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:790px;">The commercial banking business is affected not only by general<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>economic conditions, but also by the monetary policies of the </div><div id="a14995" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:805px;">Federal Reserve. Changes in the discount rate on member bank borrowing,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>availability of borrowing at the &#8220;discount window,&#8221; </div><div id="a14996" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:821px;">open market operations, changes in the Fed Funds target<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>interest rate, changes in interest rates payable on reserve accounts, the </div><div id="a14999" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:836px;">imposition of changes in reserve requirements against member banks&#8217; deposits<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and assets of foreign banking centers and the </div><div id="a15000" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:852px;">imposition of and changes in reserve requirements against certain borrowings<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>by banks and their affiliates are some of the </div><div id="a15001" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:867px;">instruments of monetary policy available to the Federal Reserve. These monetary<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>policies are used in varying combinations to </div><div id="a15002" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:882px;">influence overall growth and distributions of bank loans, investments and deposits,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>which may affect interest rates charged on </div><div id="a15004" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:897px;">loans or paid on deposits. The monetary policies of the Federal Reserve have<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>had a significant effect on the operating results of </div><div id="a15006" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:913px;">commercial banks and are expected to continue to do so in the future. The<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Federal Reserve&#8217;s policies are primarily<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>influenced by </div><div id="a15009" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:928px;">its dual mandate of price stability and full employment, and, to a lesser degree by<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>short-term and long-term changes in the </div><div id="a15014" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:944px;">international trade balance and in the fiscal policies of the U.S. Government. Future<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>changes in monetary policy and the effect of </div><div id="a15016" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:959px;">such changes on our business and earnings in the future cannot be predicted. </div></div>

<div id="a15049" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:404px;top:1022px;">23 </div><div id="a15051" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:48px;">Item 1A.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Risk Factors </div><div id="a15053" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:64px;"> </div><div id="a15054" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:62px;top:79px;">An investment in our common stock contains a high degree<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of risk. You should<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>consider carefully the following risk factors before </div><div id="a15096" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:62px;top:94px;">deciding whether to invest in our common stock. Our business, including<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>our operating results and financial condition, could be </div><div id="a15134" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:62px;top:110px;">harmed by any of these risks. Additional risks and uncertainties not currently<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>known to us or that we currently deem to be </div><div id="a15178" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:62px;top:125px;">immaterial also may materially and adversely affect our business. The trading<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>price of our common stock could decline due to </div><div id="a15218" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:62px;top:140px;">any of these risks, and you may lose all or part of your investment. In assessing these risks,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>you should also refer to the other </div><div id="a15268" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:62px;top:156px;">information contained in our filings with the SEC, including our financial<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>statements and related notes.</div><div id="a15299" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:372px;top:186px;">Market Risks </div><div id="a15304" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:217px;">We may incur losses if we are<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>unable to successfully manage interest rate risk. </div><div id="a15307" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:248px;">Our profitability depends to a large extent on Capital City Bank&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>net interest income, which is the difference between income on </div><div id="a15309" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:263px;">interest-earning assets, such as loans and investment securities, and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>expense on interest-bearing liabilities such as deposits and </div><div id="a15314" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:278px;">borrowings. We<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>are unable to predict changes in market interest rates, which are affected<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>by many factors beyond our control, </div><div id="a15316" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:294px;">including inflation, changes in trade policies by the United States or other<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>countries, such as tariffs or retaliatory tariffs, recession, </div><div id="a15320" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:309px;">unemployment, federal funds target rate, money supply,<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>domestic and international events and changes in the United States and </div><div id="a15322" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:324px;">other financial markets. Our net interest income may be reduced if: (i) more<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>interest-earning assets than interest-bearing liabilities </div><div id="a15327" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:340px;">reprice or mature during a time when interest rates are declining or (ii) more interest-bearing<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>liabilities than interest-earning assets </div><div id="a15332" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:355px;">reprice or mature during a time when interest rates are rising.<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a15335" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:386px;">Changes in the difference between short-term<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and long-term interest rates may also harm our business. We<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>generally use short-</div><div id="a15341" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:401px;">term deposits to fund longer-term assets. When interest rates change,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>assets and liabilities with shorter terms reprice more quickly </div><div id="a15344" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:416px;">than those with longer terms, which could have a material adverse effect<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>on our net interest margin. During 2022 and 2023, the </div><div id="a15346" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:432px;">Federal Reserve raised the federal funds rate 11<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>times for a cumulative increase of 5.25%. In 2024, the Federal Reserve began </div><div id="a15348" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:447px;">lowering the federal funds rate and lowered it three times during the year for a cumulative<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>decrease of 1.00%. We<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>are currently </div><div id="a15350" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:462px;">operating in an environment in which the Federal Reserve has shifted toward reducing<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>interest rates, although modestly,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>with cuts </div><div id="a15352" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:478px;">implemented in September, October<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and December 2025.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>However, the inflationary outlook remains uncertain<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and if the Federal </div><div id="a15353" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:493px;">Reserve were to further decrease interest rates, this may constrain our interest<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>rate spread due to our asset sensitivity and may </div><div id="a15358" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:508px;">adversely affect our business forecasts. On the other hand,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>rapid increases in the target federal funds rate may result in a change<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in </div><div id="a15360" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:524px;">the mix of noninterest and interest-bearing accounts and effect<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>our interest rate spread. New appointments to the Board of </div><div id="a15365" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:539px;">Governors at the Federal Reserve could result in a change in monetary policy<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and interest rates, and the potential erosion of </div><div id="a15367" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:554px;">Federal Reserve independence could negatively impact financial markets<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and impact our profitability.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>We are unable to<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>predict </div><div id="a15369" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:570px;">changes in interest rates, which are affected by factors beyond<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>our control, including inflation, deflation, recession, </div><div id="a15371" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:585px;">unemployment, money supply and other changes in financial markets. </div><div id="a15374" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:616px;">Although we continuously monitor interest rates and have a number<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of tools to manage our interest rate risk exposure, changes in </div><div id="a15377" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:631px;">market assumptions regarding future interest rates could significantly impact our<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>interest rate risk strategy, our financial<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>position </div><div id="a15379" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:646px;">and results of operations. If we do not properly monitor our interest rate risk management<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>strategies, these activities may not </div><div id="a15381" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:662px;">effectively mitigate our interest rate sensitivity or have the desired<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>impact on our results of operations or financial condition. </div><div id="a15385" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:692px;">Interest rates and economic conditions affect consumer<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>demand for housing and can create volatility in the mortgage industry.<div style="display:inline-block;width:9px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a15387" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:708px;">These risks can have a material impact on the volume of mortgage originations<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and refinancings, adversely affecting mortgage </div><div id="a15388" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:723px;">banking revenues and the profitability of our mortgage banking business.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a15392" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:754px;">See Item 7.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Financial Condition and Results of Operations under the section captioned </div><div id="a15394" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:769px;">&#8220;Net Interest Income&#8221; and &#8220;Market Risk and Interest Rate Sensitivity&#8221; elsewhere<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in this report for further discussion related to </div><div id="a15397" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:784px;">interest rate sensitivity and our management of interest rate risk. </div><div id="a15400" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:815px;">The impact of interest rates on our mortgage banking business can<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>have a significant impact on revenues.</div><div id="a15403" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:846px;">Changes in interest rates can impact our mortgage-related revenues and net revenues<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>associated with our mortgage activities.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a15406" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:735px;top:846px;letter-spacing:0.74px;">A </div><div id="a15407" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:861px;">decline in mortgage rates generally increases the demand for mortgage loans<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>as borrowers refinance, but also generally leads to </div><div id="a15409" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:876px;">accelerated payoffs. Conversely,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in a constant or increasing rate environment, we would expect fewer loans to be refinanced<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and a </div><div id="a15411" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:892px;">decline in payoffs. Although we use models to assess the impact<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of interest rates on mortgage-related revenues, the estimates of </div><div id="a15414" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:907px;">revenues produced by these models are dependent on estimates and assumptions<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of future loan demand, prepayment speeds and </div><div id="a15415" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:922px;">other factors which may differ from actual subsequent<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>experience. </div></div>
