<div id="a15419" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:404px;top:1022px;">24 </div><div id="a15421" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:48px;">Inflationary pressures and rising prices may<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>affect our results of operations and financial condition. </div><div id="a15424" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:79px;">Small to medium-sized businesses may be impacted more during periods<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of high inflation as they are not able to leverage </div><div id="a15427" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:94px;">economies of scale to mitigate cost pressures compared to larger<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>businesses. Consequently, the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>ability of our business customers </div><div id="a15429" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:110px;">to repay their loans may deteriorate, and in some cases this deterioration may occur<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>quickly, which would adversely impact<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>our </div><div id="a15431" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:125px;">results of operations and financial condition. Furthermore, a prolonged<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>period of inflation could cause wages and other costs to </div><div id="a15434" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:140px;">further increase which could adversely affect our results of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>operations and financial condition. Georgia. </div><div id="a15448" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:263px;">Our profitability and the success of our business depends substantially on the general<div Unlike larger national or other regional </div><div id="a15452" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:294px;">banks that are more geographically diversified, we provide banking<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and financial services primarily to customers across northern </div><div id="a15454" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:309px;">Florida and Georgia. The local economic conditions in<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>these areas have a significant impact on the demand for our products and </div><div id="a15456" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:324px;">services as well as the ability of our customers to repay loans, the value of the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>collateral securing loans and the stability of our </div><div id="a15459" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:340px;">deposit funding sources. As a result, a significant decline in general economic<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>conditions in Florida or Georgia, whether caused </div><div id="a15461" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:355px;">by recession, inflation, unemployment, in-flows and out-flows of residents,<div occurrences or other </div><div id="a15468" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:386px;">factors could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial<div results of operations.</div><div id="a15474" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:447px;">Individual,<div Such principles require that unrealized </div><div id="a15506" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:616px;">gains and losses in the estimated value of the available-for-sale<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>portfolio be &#8220;marked to market&#8221; and reflected as a separate item in </div><div id="a15513" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:631px;">shareowners&#8217; equity (net of tax) as accumulated other comprehensive<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>income/losses. Shareowners&#8217; equity will continue to reflect </div><div id="a15515" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:646px;">the unrealized gains and losses (net of tax) of these investments. The fair value<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of our investment portfolio may decline, causing a </div><div id="a15517" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:662px;">corresponding decline in shareowners&#8217; equity. </div><div id="a15520" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:692px;">Management believes that several factors will affect the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>fair values of our investment portfolio. These include, but are not limited </div><div id="a15522" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:708px;">to, changes in interest rates or expectations of changes in interest rates, the degree<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of volatility in the securities markets, inflation </div><div id="a15524" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:723px;">rates or expectations of inflation and the slope of the interest rate yield curve<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>(the yield curve refers to the differences between </div><div id="a15526" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:738px;">short-term and long-term interest rates; a positively sloped yield curve means short<div style="display:inline-block;width:1px">&#160;</div>-term rates are lower than long-term rates). </div><div id="a15535" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:754px;">These and other factors may impact specific categories of the portfolio differently,<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>and we cannot predict the effect these factors </div><div id="a15537" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:769px;">may have on any specific category. </div><div id="a15540" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:800px;">Shares of our common stock are not an insured<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>deposit and may lose value.</div><div id="a15543" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:830px;">The shares of our common stock are not a bank deposit and will not be insured or guaranteed<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>by the FDIC or any other </div><div id="a15544" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:846px;">government agency.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Your<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>investment will be subject to investment risk, and you must be capable of affording the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>loss of your </div><div id="a15545" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:861px;">entire investment. </div><div id="a15548" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:892px;">Limited trading activity for shares of our common stock may<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>contribute to price volatility. </div><div id="a15551" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:922px;">While our common stock is listed and traded on the Nasdaq Global Select Market, there<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>has historically been limited trading </div><div id="a15552" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:938px;">activity in our common stock.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>The average daily trading volume of our common stock over the 12-month<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>period ending </div><div id="a15555" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:953px;">December 31, 2025 was approximately 37,371 shares. Due to the limited<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>trading activity of our common stock, relativity small </div><div id="a15564" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:968px;">trades may have a significant impact on the price of our common stock. Similarly,<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>significant sales of our common stock, or the </div><div id="a15566" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:984px;">expectation of these sales, could cause our stock prices to fall. </div></div>

<div id="a15569" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:404px;top:1022px;">25 </div><div id="a15572" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:64px;">Securities analysts may not initiate coverage or continue to cover our common<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>stock, and this may have a negative impact </div><div id="a15573" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:79px;">on its market price. </div><div id="a15576" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:110px;">The trading market for our common stock will depend in part on the research<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and reports that securities analysts publish about us </div><div id="a15578" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:125px;">and our business. We do<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>not have any control over securities analysts, and they may not initiate coverage<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or continue to cover our </div><div id="a15580" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:140px;">common stock. If any securities analysts covering our common stock publishes<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>an unfavorable report, our stock price would </div><div id="a15581" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:156px;">likely decline. If one or more of analysts covering our common stock ceases to cover<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>our Company or fails to publish regular </div><div id="a15582" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:171px;">reports on us, the lack of research coverage and lose of visibility in the financial<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>markets may cause our stock price or trading </div><div id="a15584" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:186px;">volume to decline. </div><div id="a15587" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:375px;top:217px;">Credit Risks </div><div id="a15590" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:248px;">Our loan portfolio includes loans with a higher risk of loss which could lead to higher loan losses and nonperforming </div><div id="a15591" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:263px;">assets.</div><div id="a15594" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:294px;">We originate<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>commercial real estate loans, commercial loans, construction loans, vacant land<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>loans, consumer loans, and </div><div id="a15595" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:309px;">residential mortgage loans primarily within our market area. Commercial<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>real estate, commercial, construction, vacant land, and </div><div id="a15597" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:324px;">consumer loans may expose a lender to greater credit risk than traditional<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>fixed-rate fully amortizing loans secured by residential </div><div id="a15600" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:340px;">real estate because the collateral securing these loans may not be sold as easily as residential<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>real estate. In addition, these loan </div><div id="a15602" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:355px;">types tend to involve larger loan balances to a single borrower or<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>groups of related borrowers and are more susceptible to a risk of </div><div id="a15604" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:370px;">loss during a downturn in the business cycle. These loans also have historically<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>had greater credit risk than other loans for the </div><div id="a15607" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:386px;">following reasons: </div><div id="a15610" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:86px;top:417px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a15612" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:110px;top:417px;">Commercial Real Estate Loans</div><div id="a15613" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:287px;top:417px;">. Repayment is dependent on income being generated in amounts sufficient<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to cover </div><div id="a15614" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:433px;">operating expenses and debt service. These loans also involve greater risk because<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>they are generally not fully amortizing </div><div id="a15615" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:448px;">over the loan period, but rather have a balloon payment due at maturity.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>A borrower&#8217;s ability to make a balloon payment </div><div id="a15616" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:463px;">typically will depend on the borrower&#8217;s ability to either refinance<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the loan or timely sell the underlying property.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Further, </div><div id="a15618" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:479px;">these loans generally are more affected by adverse conditions in the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>economy. Because payments<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>on loans secured by </div><div id="a15619" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:494px;">commercial real estate often depend upon the successful operation and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>management of the properties and the businesses </div><div id="a15620" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:509px;">which operate from within them, repayment of such loans may be affected<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>by factors outside the borrower&#8217;s control, </div><div id="a15621" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:525px;">such as adverse conditions in the real estate market or the economy or changes<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in government regulations.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>At December </div><div id="a15622" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:540px;">31, 2025, commercial mortgage loans comprised approximately<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>30.2% of our total loan portfolio.<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a15631" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:86px;top:572px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a15633" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:110px;top:572px;">Commercial Loans</div><div id="a15634" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:219px;top:572px;">. Repayment is generally dependent upon the successful operation of the borrower&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>business. In </div><div id="a15635" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:587px;">addition, the collateral securing the loans may depreciate over time, be<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>difficult to appraise, be illiquid, or fluctuate in </div><div id="a15636" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:602px;">value based on the success of the business. These loans are also sensitive to broader<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>economic conditions, competitive </div><div id="a15638" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:618px;">pressures, and industry-specific trends, any of which may disproportionately<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>impact certain segments during periods of </div><div id="a15641" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:633px;">stress and increase the likelihood of credit deterioration.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>At December 31, 2025, commercial loans comprised </div><div id="a15647" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:648px;">approximately 7.1% of our total loan portfolio. </div><div id="a15650" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:86px;top:680px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a15652" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:110px;top:680px;">Construction Loans</div><div id="a15653" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:223px;top:680px;">. The risk of loss is largely dependent on our initial estimate of whether<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the property&#8217;s value at </div><div id="a15654" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:695px;">completion equals or exceeds the cost of property construction and the availability<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of take-out financing. During the </div><div id="a15657" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:711px;">construction phase, a number of factors can result in delays or cost overruns. If<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>our estimate is inaccurate or if actual </div><div id="a15658" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:726px;">construction costs exceed estimates,</div><div id="a15660" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:307px;top:726px;">which could be impacted by factors outside of our control, including<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>tariff, trade, </div><div id="a15661" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:741px;">and immigration policies, the value of the property securing our<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>loan may be insufficient to ensure full repayment when </div><div id="a15664" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:757px;">completed through a permanent loan, sale of the property,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or by seizure of collateral.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>At December 31, 2025, </div><div id="a15667" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:772px;">construction loans comprised approximately 5.8% of our total loan<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>portfolio. </div><div id="a15674" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:86px;top:804px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a15676" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:110px;top:804px;">Vacant<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Land Loans</div><div id="a15677" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:223px;top:804px;">. These loans<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>are susceptible to adverse </div><div id="a15680" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:850px;">conditions in the real estate market and local economy.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>At December 31, 2025, vacant land loans comprised </div><div id="a15683" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:865px;">approximately 3.8% of our total loan portfolio. </div><div id="a15688" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:86px;top:896px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a15690" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:110px;top:896px;">HELOCs</div><div id="a15691" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:164px;top:896px;">. Our open-ended home equity loans have an interest-only draw period<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>followed by a five-year repayment </div><div id="a15698" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:912px;">period of 0.75% of the principal balance monthly and a balloon payment<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>at maturity. Upon the commencement<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of the </div><div id="a15699" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:927px;">repayment period, the monthly payment can increase significantly,<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>thus, there is a heightened risk that the borrower will </div><div id="a15700" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:943px;">be unable to pay the increased payment. Further,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>these loans also involve greater risk because they are generally not fully </div><div id="a15701" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:958px;">amortizing over the loan period but rather have a balloon payment due at maturity.<div style="display:inline-block;width:9px">&#160;</div>A borrower&#8217;s ability to make a </div><div id="a15702" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:973px;">balloon payment may depend on the borrower&#8217;s ability<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to either refinance the loan or timely sell the underlying property.<div style="display:inline-block;width:9px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a15703" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:989px;">At December 31, 2025, HELOCs comprised approximately 9.5% of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>our total loan portfolio. </div></div>

<div id="Page26" style="background-color:RGB(255, 255, 255);position:relative;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;overflow:hidden;border-style:solid;border-width:thin;border-color:RGB(198, 198, 198);page-break-after:always;width:816px;height:1056px;">
<div id="a15712" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:404px;top:1022px;">26 </div><div id="a15715" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:86px;top:65px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a15717" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:110px;top:65px;">Consumer Loans</div><div id="a15718" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:208px;top:65px;">. Consumer loans (such as automobile loans and personal lines of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>credit) are collateralized, if at all, </div><div id="a15719" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:80px;">with assets that may not provide an adequate source of payment of the loan due<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to depreciation, damage, or loss. At </div><div id="a15720" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:95px;">December 31, 2025, consumer loans comprised approximately 7.2%<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of our total loan portfolio, with indirect auto loans </div><div id="a15725" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:110px;top:111px;">making up a majority of this portfolio at approximately 85.9% of the total balance. </div><div id="a15730" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:141px;">The increased risks associated with these types of loans result in a correspondingly<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>higher probability of default on such loans (as </div><div id="a15732" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:157px;">compared to fixed-rate fully amortizing single-family real estate loans).<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>Loan defaults would likely increase our loan losses and </div><div id="a15737" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:172px;">nonperforming assets and could adversely affect our allowance<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>for credit losses and our results of operations.</div><div id="a15738" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:16px;left:646px;top:169px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a15740" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:654px;top:172px;">In addition, credit </div><div id="a15741" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:187px;">risk may be elevated by borrower or third party fraud, inaccuracies in financial<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>information, or misrepresentations in loan </div><div id="a15742" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:203px;">documentation. As seen across the banking industry,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>evolving fraud schemes and greater digitization of financial transactions can </div><div id="a15745" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:218px;">increase the risk that loans are underwritten based on incomplete, inaccurate,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or falsified information, which may heighten the risk </div><div id="a15747" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:233px;">of unexpected credit losses. </div><div id="a15750" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:264px;">Our loan portfolio is heavily concentrated in mortgage loans secured<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>by properties in Florida and Georgia which causes </div><div id="a15751" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:279px;">our risk of loss to be higher than if we had a more geographically diversified<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>portfolio.<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a15754" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:310px;">Our interest-earning assets are heavily concentrated in mortgage loans secured<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>by real estate, particularly real estate located in </div><div id="a15758" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:325px;">Florida and Georgia.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>At December 31, 2025, approximately 85.7% of our loans included real estate as a primary,<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>secondary, or </div><div id="a15763" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:341px;">tertiary component of collateral. The real estate collateral in each case provides<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>an alternate source of repayment in the event of </div><div id="a15766" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:356px;">default by the borrower; however, the value<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of the collateral may decline during the time the credit is extended. If we are required </div><div id="a15768" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:371px;">to liquidate the collateral securing a loan during a period of reduced real estate values<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to satisfy the debt, our earnings and capital </div><div id="a15770" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:387px;">could be adversely affected. </div><div id="a15773" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:417px;">Additionally, at December<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>31, 2025, a significant number of our loans secured by real estate are secured by commercial and </div><div id="a15776" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:433px;">residential properties located in Florida and Georgia. The<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>concentration of our loans in these areas subjects us to risk that a </div><div id="a15779" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:448px;">downturn in the economy or recession in these areas could result in a decrease in<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>loan originations and increases in delinquencies </div><div id="a15781" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:463px;">and foreclosures, which would more greatly affect us than<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>if our lending were more geographically diversified. In addition, since </div><div id="a15783" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:479px;">a large portion of our portfolio is secured by properties located<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in Florida and Georgia, the occurrence of a natural disaster,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>such </div><div id="a15785" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:494px;">as a hurricane, or a man-made disaster could result in a decline in loan originations,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a decline in the value or destruction of </div><div id="a15788" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:509px;">mortgaged properties and an increase in the risk of delinquencies, foreclosures<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or loss on loans originated by us. Severe weather </div><div id="a15790" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:525px;">events, catastrophic natural disasters, or other large-scale<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>disruptions may also rapidly impair collateral values and borrower </div><div id="a15793" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:540px;">repayment capacity across an entire geographic market, increasing both<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>credit losses and required credit-loss reserves. We<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>may </div><div id="a15797" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:555px;">suffer further losses due to the decline in the value of the properties underlying<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>our mortgage loans, which would have an adverse </div><div id="a15799" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:571px;">impact on our results of operations and financial condition. </div><div id="a15802" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:601px;">Our concentration in loans secured by real estate<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>may increase our credit losses, which would negatively<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>affect our </div><div id="a15803" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:617px;">financial results.<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a15806" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:647px;">Due to the lack of diversified industry within some of the markets served by CCB and the relatively<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>close proximity of our </div><div id="a15807" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:663px;">geographic markets, we have both geographic concentrations as well as concentrations<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in the types of loans funded. Specifically, </div><div id="a15809" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:678px;">due to the nature of our markets, a significant portion of the portfolio has historically<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>been secured with real estate. At December </div><div id="a15811" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:693px;">31, 2025, approximately 31.5% and 54.2% of our $2.546 billion loan<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>portfolio was secured by commercial real estate and </div><div id="a15823" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:709px;">residential real estate, respectively.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>As of this same date, approximately 5.8% was secured by property under construction.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Due to </div><div id="a15831" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:724px;">the exposure in these concentrations, disruptions in markets, economic<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>conditions, changes in laws or regulations or other events </div><div id="a15834" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:739px;">could cause a significant impact on the ability of borrowers to repay and may<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>have a material adverse effect on our business, </div><div id="a15836" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:755px;">financial condition and results of operations. </div><div id="a15839" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:785px;">In weak economies, or in areas where real estate market conditions are distressed,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>we may experience a higher than normal level </div><div id="a15841" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:801px;">of nonperforming real estate loans. The collateral value of the portfolio and the revenue stream<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>from those loans could come </div><div id="a15842" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:816px;">under stress, and additional provisions for the allowance for credit losses could<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>be necessitated. In the event we are required to </div><div id="a15844" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:831px;">foreclose on a property securing one of our mortgage loans or otherwise pursue<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>our remedies in order to protect our investment, </div><div id="a15846" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:847px;">we may be unable to recover funds in an amount equal to our projected return<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>on our investment or in an amount sufficient to </div><div id="a15847" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:862px;">prevent a loss to us due to prevailing economic conditions, real estate values and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>other factors associated with the ownership of </div><div id="a15849" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:877px;">real property. As a result,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the market value of the real estate or other collateral underlying our loans may not, at any given<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>time, be </div><div id="a15851" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:893px;">sufficient to satisfy the outstanding principal amount of the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>loans, and consequently, we would<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>sustain loan losses. </div></div>

<div id="a16946" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:404px;top:1022px;">36 </div><div id="a16948" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:368px;top:48px;">Strategic Risks</div><div id="a16951" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:79px;">Our future success is dependent on our ability to compete effectively<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in the highly competitive banking and financial </div><div id="a16952" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:94px;">services industry. </div><div id="a16955" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:123px;">We face vigorous<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>competition for deposits, loans and other financial services in our market area<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>from other banks and financial </div><div id="a16957" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:139px;">institutions, including savings and loan associations, savings banks,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>finance companies and credit unions. A number of our </div><div id="a16958" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:154px;">competitors are significantly larger than we are and have greater access to<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>capital and other resources. Many of our competitors </div><div id="a16960" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:170px;">also have higher lending limits, more expansive branch networks, and offer<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a wider array of financial products and services.<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a16963" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:200px;">We also compete<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>with other non-bank providers of financial services, such as money market mutual<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>funds, brokerage firms, </div><div id="a16966" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:215px;">consumer finance companies, insurance companies, governmental<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>organizations, and non-bank financial technology and wealth </div><div id="a16969" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:231px;">technology providers, including digital asset service providers. Many of our<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>non-bank competitors are not subject to the same </div><div id="a16972" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:246px;">extensive regulations that govern our activities. As a result, these non-bank<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>competitors have advantages over us in providing </div><div id="a16975" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:262px;">certain services, including the ability to offer financial products and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>services on more favorable terms than we are able to offer. </div><div id="a16977" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:277px;">Technology<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and other changes have lowered barriers to entry and made it possible for non-banks to<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>offer products and services </div><div id="a16980" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:292px;">traditionally provided by banks. In particular,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the activity of financial technology companies has grown significantly over recent </div><div id="a16982" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:307px;">years and is expected to continue to grow.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>The emergence, adoption and evolution of new technologies that do<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>not require </div><div id="a16983" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:323px;">intermediation, including distributed ledgers such as digital assets and blockchain,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>as well as advances in robotic process </div><div id="a16984" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:338px;">automation, could significantly affect the competition<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>for financial services. <div id="Page58" style="background-color:RGB(255, 255, 255);position:relative;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;overflow:hidden;border-style:solid;border-width:thin;border-color:RGB(198, 198, 198);page-break-after:always;width:816px;height:1056px;">
<div id="a26241" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:404px;top:1022px;">58 </div><div id="a26243" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:62px;top:48px;">Nonaccrual Loans</div><div id="a26244" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:161px;top:48px;">.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Nonaccrual loans totaled $8.6 million at December 31, 2025, a $2.3 million increase<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>over December 31, 2024 </div><div id="a26262" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:64px;">with the increase primarily attributable to two home equity loans totaling<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>$1.8 million.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Generally, loans are placed on<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>nonaccrual </div><div id="a26266" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:79px;">status if principal or interest payments become 90 days past due or management<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>deems the collectability of the principal and </div><div id="a26267" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:94px;">interest to be doubtful.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Once a loan is placed in nonaccrual status, all previously accrued and uncollected<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>interest is reversed </div><div id="a26269" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:110px;">against interest income.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Interest income on nonaccrual loans is recognized when the ultimate collectability is no<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>longer </div><div id="a26270" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:125px;">considered doubtful.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Loans are returned to accrual status when the principal and interest amounts contractually due<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>are brought </div><div id="a26272" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:140px;">current or when future payments are reasonably assured.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>If interest on our loans classified as nonaccrual during 2025 had been </div><div id="a26277" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:156px;">recognized on a fully accruing basis, we would have recorded an additional<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>$0.4 million of interest income for the year ended </div><div id="a26284" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:171px;">December 31, 2025. </div><div id="a26290" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:62px;top:202px;">Other Real Estate Owned</div><div id="a26291" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:199px;top:202px;">.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>OREO represents property acquired as the result of borrower defaults on<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>loans or by receiving a deed </div><div id="a26292" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:217px;">in lieu of foreclosure.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>OREO is recorded at the lower of cost or estimated fair value, less estimated selling costs, at the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>time of </div><div id="a26294" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:232px;">foreclosure.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Write-downs occurring at foreclosure are<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>charged against the allowance for credit losses.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>On an ongoing basis, </div><div id="a26300" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:248px;">properties are either revalued internally or by a third-party appraiser<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>as required by applicable regulations.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Subsequent declines in </div><div id="a26303" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:263px;">value are reflected as other noninterest expense.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>Carrying costs related to maintaining the OREO properties are expensed as </div><div id="a26305" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:278px;">incurred and are also reflected as other noninterest expense. </div><div id="a26308" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:309px;">OREO totaled $1.9 million at December 31, 2025, versus $0.4 million<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>at December 31, 2024.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>During 2025, we added properties </div><div id="a26335" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:324px;">totaling $4.4 million and sold properties totaling $2.9 million.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>For 2024, we added properties totaling $1.0 million and sold </div><div id="a26385" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:340px;">properties totaling $0.6 million. </div><div id="a26398" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:62px;top:370px;">Modifications to Borrowers Experiencing<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Financial Difficulty</div><div id="a26399" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:394px;top:370px;">.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Occasionally, we will modify<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>loans to borrowers who are </div><div id="a26400" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:386px;">experiencing financial difficulty.<div style="display:inline-block;width:9px">&#160;</div>Loan modifications to borrowers in financial difficulty are loans in<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>which we will grant an </div><div id="a26402" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:401px;">economic concession to the borrower that we would not otherwise consider.<div style="display:inline-block;width:9px">&#160;</div>In these instances, as part of a work-out alternative, </div><div id="a26405" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:416px;">we will make concessions including the extension of the loan term, a principal<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>moratorium, a reduction in the interest rate, or a </div><div id="a26407" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:432px;">combination thereof.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>A modified loan classification can be removed if the borrower&#8217;s financial condition<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>improves such that the </div><div id="a26410" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:447px;">borrower is no longer in financial difficulty,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the loan has not had any forgiveness of principal or interest, and the loan is </div><div id="a26412" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:462px;">subsequently refinanced or restructured at market terms and qualifies as a new<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>loan.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>At December 31, 2025, we maintained four </div><div id="a26417" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:478px;">loans for $3.8 million that we modified due to the borrower experiencing<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>financial difficulty.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a26427" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:62px;top:508px;">Past Due Loans</div><div id="a26428" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:148px;top:508px;">.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>A loan is defined as a past due loan when one full payment is past due or a contractual maturity<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>is over 30 days </div><div id="a26430" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:524px;">past due.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Past due loans at December 31, 2025 totaled $7.0 million compared to $4.3 million<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>at December 31, 2024.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Indirect </div><div id="a26450" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:539px;">auto loans represented a large portion of the past due balances representing<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>26% and 56%, respectively,<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div>of the total dollars past </div><div id="a26461" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:554px;">due at December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, respectively.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a26469" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:570px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:27px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a26471" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:62px;top:585px;">Potential Problem Loans</div><div id="a26472" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:197px;top:585px;">.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Potential problem loans are defined as those loans which are now current but where management<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>has </div><div id="a26473" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:600px;">doubt as to the borrower&#8217;s ability to comply with present<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>loan repayment terms.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>At December 31, 2025, we had $4.7 million in </div><div id="a26485" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:616px;">loans of this type which were not included in either of the nonaccrual or<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>90 days past due loan categories compared to $2.8 </div><div id="a26496" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:631px;">million at December 31, 2024.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Management monitors these loans closely and reviews their performance<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>on a regular basis. </div><div id="a26502" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:646px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:30px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a26504" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:62px;top:662px;">Loan Concentrations</div><div id="a26505" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:176px;top:662px;">.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Loan concentrations exist when there are amounts loaned to multiple borrowers engaged<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in similar </div><div id="a26506" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:677px;">activities which cause them to be similarly impacted by economic or other conditions<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and such amount exceeds 10% of our total </div><div id="a26509" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:692px;">loans.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Due to the lack of diversified industry within our markets and the relatively<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>close proximity of the markets, we have both </div><div id="a26511" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:708px;">geographic concentrations as well as concentrations in the types of loans funded.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>Specifically, due to the nature of our markets,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a </div><div id="a26513" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:723px;">significant portion of our HFI loan portfolio has historically been<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>secured with real estate, approximately 86% at December 31, </div><div id="a26519" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:738px;">2025 and 85% at December 31, 2024, with the increase driven by lower loan volume<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in 2025<div style="display:inline-block;width:3px">&#160;</div>for commercial and consumer </div><div id="a26533" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:754px;">(indirect auto) loans and a higher volume of 1-4 family residential real estate loans<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>originated in 2025 in comparison to other loan </div><div id="a26540" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:769px;">types.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>The primary types of real estate collateral are commercial properties and 1-4 family<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>residential properties. </div><div id="a26545" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:800px;">We review our<div as needed to </div><div id="a26546" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:815px;">mitigate/reduce risk to segments that reflect decline or stress.<div </div><div id="a27127" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:757px;">Allowance for Credit Losses </div><div id="a27133" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:787px;">The allowance for credit losses is a valuation account that is deducted from<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the loans&#8217; amortized cost basis to present the net </div><div id="a27177" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:803px;">amount expected to be collected on the loans.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>The allowance for credit losses is adjusted by a credit loss provision which is </div><div id="a27221" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:818px;">reported in earnings and reduced by the charge-off<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of loan amounts, net of recoveries.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Loans are charged off against the </div><div id="a27263" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:833px;">allowance when management believes the uncollectability of a loan<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>balance is confirmed.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Expected recoveries do not exceed the </div><div id="a27299" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:849px;">aggregate of amounts previously charged-off<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and expected to be charged-off.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>Expected credit loss inherent in non-cancellable </div><div id="a27337" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:864px;">off-balance sheet credit exposures is provided through the credit<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>loss provision but recorded separately in other liabilities. </div><div id="a27376" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:895px;">Management estimates the allowance balance using relevant available<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>information, from internal and external sources, relating to </div><div id="a27408" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:910px;">past events, current conditions, and reasonable and supportable forecasts.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>Historical loan default and loss experience provides the </div><div id="a27442" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:925px;">basis for the estimation of expected credit losses.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>Adjustments to historical loss information incorporate management&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>view of </div><div id="a27476" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:941px;">current conditions and forecasts.<div style="display:inline-block;width:14px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a27486" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:971px;">Detailed information regarding the methodology for estimating<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the amount reported in the allowance for credit losses is provided </div><div id="a27522" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:987px;">in Note 1 &#8211; Significant Accounting Policies/Allowance for Credit Losses in<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the Consolidated Financial Statements. </div></div>

<div id="Page64" style="background-color:RGB(255, 255, 255);position:relative;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;overflow:hidden;border-style:solid;border-width:thin;border-color:RGB(198, 198, 198);page-break-after:always;width:816px;height:1056px;">
<div id="a30417" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:404px;top:1022px;">64 </div><div id="a30419" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:48px;">Market Risk and Interest Rate Sensitivity</div><div id="a30422" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:62px;top:79px;">Overview.</div><div id="a30423" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:117px;top:79px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a30424" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:123px;top:79px;">Market risk arises from changes in interest rates, exchange rates,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>commodity prices, and equity prices.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>We have risk </div><div id="a30427" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:94px;">management policies designed to monitor and limit exposure to market<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>risk and we do not participate in activities that give rise to </div><div id="a30429" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:110px;">significant market risk involving exchange rates, commodity prices, or<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>equity prices.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>In asset and liability management activities, </div><div id="a30432" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:125px;">our policies are designed to minimize structural interest rate risk. </div><div id="a30435" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:62px;top:156px;">Interest Rate Risk Management.</div><div id="a30436" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:234px;top:156px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a30437" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:240px;top:156px;">Our net income is largely dependent on net interest income.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>Net interest income is susceptible to </div><div id="a30440" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:171px;">interest rate risk to the degree that interest-bearing liabilities mature<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or reprice on a different basis than interest-earning </div><div id="a30445" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:186px;">assets.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>When interest-bearing liabilities mature or reprice more quickly than interest-earning<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>assets in a given period, a significant </div><div id="a30452" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:202px;">increase in market rates of interest could adversely affect net interest income.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>Similarly, when interest-earning<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>assets mature or </div><div id="a30457" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:217px;">reprice more quickly than interest-bearing liabilities, falling market interest<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>rates could result in a decrease in net interest </div><div id="a30460" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:232px;">income.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Net interest income is also affected by changes in the portion of interest-earning<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>assets that are funded by interest-</div><div id="a30466" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:248px;">bearing liabilities rather than by other sources of funds, such as noninterest<div style="display:inline-block;width:1px">&#160;</div>-bearing deposits and shareowners&#8217; equity. </div><div id="a30471" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:278px;">We have established<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>what we believe to be a comprehensive interest rate risk management policy,<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>which is administered by </div><div id="a30472" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:294px;">management&#8217;s Asset Liability Management<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Committee (&#8220;ALCO&#8221;).<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>The policy establishes limits of risk, which are quantitative </div><div id="a30475" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:309px;">measures of the percentage change in net interest income (a measure of net<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>interest income at risk) and the fair value of equity </div><div id="a30477" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:324px;">capital (a measure of economic value of equity (&#8220;EVE&#8221;) at risk) resulting from<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a hypothetical change in interest rates for </div><div id="a30478" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:340px;">maturities from one day to 30 years.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>We measure the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>potential adverse impacts that changing interest rates may have on our </div><div id="a30481" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:355px;">short-term earnings, long-term value, and liquidity by employing<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>simulation analysis through the use of computer modeling.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a30489" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:386px;">The Company&#8217;s interest rate risk sensitivity<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>simulations apply various behavior models and assumptions to account<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>for customer </div><div id="a30492" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:401px;">tendencies stemming from interest rate risk changes. The key behavior<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>models and assumptions incorporated in the NII and EVE </div><div id="a30496" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:416px;">simulations impact deposit pricing, deposit runoff,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>time deposit early withdrawal, and prepayments on loans and investments. The </div><div id="a30501" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:432px;">deposit pricing model is one of the most significant of these assumptions and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>determines to what degree our deposit rates change </div><div id="a30504" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:447px;">when benchmark interest rates change. The deposit runoff<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>model reflects the increased attrition rate observed in noninterest </div><div id="a30507" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:462px;">bearing deposits in higher rate scenarios as customers migrate to interest bearing<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>deposits and/or alternative investments. The time </div><div id="a30510" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:478px;">deposit early withdrawal model incorporates the customer&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>ability to early terminate time deposits and reprice higher.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>The </div><div id="a30517" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:493px;">prepayment models applied to loans and investments reflects the incentive<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>borrowers have to refinance when market rates are low </div><div id="a30520" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:508px;">while conversely slowing down their payments in higher rate environments.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Each of the models and assumptions are tailored to </div><div id="a30523" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:524px;">the specific interest rate environment and validated on a regular basis. However,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>assumptions and models are inherently uncertain </div><div id="a30525" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:539px;">and actual results may differ from those derived in simulation analysis<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>for multiple reasons, which may include actual balance </div><div id="a30528" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:554px;">sheet composition differences, timing, magnitude<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and frequency of interest rate changes, deviations from projected customer </div><div id="a30531" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:570px;">behavioral assumptions, and changes in market conditions or management<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>strategies. </div><div id="a30537" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:616px;">The statement of financial condition is subject to testing for both parallel and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>non-parallel upward and downward shifts in interest </div><div id="a30547" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:631px;">rates (assuming no balance sheet growth) to indicate the inherent interest<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>rate risk.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>We prepare a base<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>case (assumes a static rate </div><div id="a30555" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:646px;">environment) and several alternative interest rate simulations for<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>various ranges of upward and downward interest rate changes.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a30562" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:662px;">This analysis is prepared quarterly and reported to ALCO, our Market<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Risk Oversight Committee (&#8220;MROC&#8221;), our Risk Oversight </div><div id="a30567" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:677px;">Committee (&#8220;ROC&#8221;) and the Board of Directors.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>We will periodically<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>augment our interest rate simulations with alternative </div><div id="a30572" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:692px;">interest rate scenarios that may include various non-parallel shifts in interest rates,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>including a flattening or steepening of the yield </div><div id="a30577" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:708px;">curve.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a30580" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:738px;">Our goal is to structure the statement of financial condition so that net interest earnings at risk over<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>12-month and 24-month </div><div id="a30585" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:754px;">periods and the economic value of equity at risk do not exceed policy guidelines<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>at the various interest rate shock levels.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>We </div><div id="a30587" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:769px;">attempt to achieve this goal by balancing, within policy limits, the volume<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of floating-rate liabilities with a similar volume of </div><div id="a30590" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:784px;">floating-rate assets, by keeping the average maturity of fixed-rate asset and liability<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>contracts reasonably matched, by managing </div><div id="a30595" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:800px;">the mix of our core deposits, and by adjusting our rates to market conditions on<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a continuing basis.<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a30597" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:815px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:116px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a30599" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:62px;top:830px;">Analysis.</div><div id="a30600" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:111px;top:830px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a30601" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:118px;top:830px;">Measures of net interest income at risk produced by simulation analysis are<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>indicators of an institution&#8217;s short-term </div><div id="a30604" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:846px;">performance in alternative rate environments.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>These measures are typically based upon a relatively brief period, and do not </div><div id="a30607" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:861px;">necessarily indicate the long-term prospects or economic value of the institution.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>The following table presents our net interest </div><div id="a30611" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:876px;">income simulation results for gradual 12-month and 24-month &#8220;ramp&#8221;<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>scenarios applied to base scenario.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>The &#8220;ramp&#8221; scenario is </div><div id="a30626" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:892px;">a parallel shift applied gradually over a 12-month period for the projected<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>12-month and 24-month period on a pro rata basis.<div style="display:inline-block;width:11px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a30640" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:907px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:3px">&#160;</div></div></div>

</div><div id="a32447" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:186px;">unrecognized actuarial amounts.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>The most $0.5 </div><div id="a32495" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:324px;">million decrease or increase, respectively.<div style="display:inline-block;width:9px">&#160;</div>We anticipate using<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a 5.67% discount rate in 2026.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a32508" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:355px;">Based on the balances at the December 31, 2025 approximately $3.2 </div><div id="a32595" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:386px;">million (after-tax).<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>The gains on AFS securities are excluded from earnings and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>reported, net of tax, in other comprehensive income.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>For AFS </div><div id="a37703" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:46px;">securities that are in an unrealized loss present value of cash flows to </div><div id="a38013" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:153px;">be collected from the security are compared to the amortized cost losses is recorded </div><div id="a38103" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:184px;">through a provision for credit loss expense, limited by the amount that fair<div style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:199px;">impairment that is not credit related is recognized in other comprehensive<div
