style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:261px;">Management measures expected credit losses on each individual HTM debt<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>security that has not been deemed to have a zero </div><div id="a38232" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:276px;">assumption.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Each security that is not deemed to have zero credit losses is individually measured<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>based on net realizable value, or </div><div id="a38274" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:291px;">the difference between the discounted value<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of the expected cash flows, based on the original effective rate, and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the recorded </div><div id="a38314" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:307px;">amortized basis of the security.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>To the extent a shortfall is related<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to credit loss, an allowance for credit loss is recorded through a </div><div id="a38362" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:322px;">provision for credit loss expense. See Note 2 &#8211; Investment Securities for<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>additional information.</div></div></div></ix:continuation></div><div id="TextContainer84" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:4px;top:0px;">Loans Held for Investment</div><div id="a38395" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:31px;">Loans held for investment (&#8220;HFI&#8221;) are stated at amortized cost which includes<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the principal amount outstanding, net premiums </div><div id="a38431" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:46px;">and discounts, and net deferred loan fees and costs.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>Accrued interest receivable on loans is reported in other assets and is not </div><div id="a38475" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>Fees charged to originate loans and direct loan origination<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>costs are deferred and </div><div id="a38627" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:138px;">accrual of interest is generally suspended on loans more than 90 days past<div when the ultimate collectability is no longer considered doubtful.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>Loans are returned to accrual status when the </div><div id="a38791" id="a38943" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:276px;">(if applicable), and collateral value.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Charge-off decisions for consumer loans<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>are dictated by the Federal Financial Institutions </div><div id="a38980" Account Management Policy which establishes<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>standards for the </div><div id="a39010" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:307px;">classification and treatment of consumer loans, which generally require<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>charge-off after 120 days of delinquency. </div><div id="a39043" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:337px;">The Company has adopted comprehensive lending policies, underwriting<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>standards and loan review procedures designed to </div><div id="a39073" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New See Note 3 &#8211; Loans Held for Investment<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and Allowance for Credit Losses for </div><div id="a39220" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:414px;">additional information.</div></div></div></ix:nonNumeric></div><div id="TextContainer85" style="position:relative;width:713px;z-index:1;"><div id="a39220_23_4" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:127px;top:767px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:10px">&#160;</div></div></div><div id="div_81_XBRL_TS_e0b7b7212f8a4a26a427098ff7f60c8b" style="position:absolute;left:0px;top:797px;float:left;"><ix:nonNumeric id="ID_1113" name="us-gaap:LoansAndLeasesReceivableAllowanceForLoanLossesPolicy" contextRef="FROM_Jan01_2025_TO_Dec31_2025_Entity_0000726601" continuedAt="XBRL_TS_e0b7b7212f8a4a26a427098ff7f60c8b_1" escape="true"><div id="TextBlockContainer82" style="position:relative;line-height:normal;width:707px;height:138px;"><div id="TextContainer82" style="position:relative;width:707px;z-index:1;"><div id="a39228" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:4px;top:0px;">Allowance for Credit Losses</div><div id="a39234" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:31px;">The allowance for credit losses is a valuation account that is deducted from<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the loans&#8217; id="TextBlockContainer90" style="position:relative;line-height:normal;width:711px;height:696px;"><div id="TextContainer90" style="position:relative;width:711px;z-index:1;"><div id="a39481" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:0px;">Management estimates the allowance balance using relevant available<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>information, from internal and external sources, relating to </div><div id="a39513" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:15px;">past events, current conditions, and reasonable and supportable forecasts.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>Historical loan default and loss experience provides the </div><div id="a39547" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:31px;">basis for the estimation of expected credit losses.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>Adjustments to historical loss information incorporate management&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>view of </div><div id="a39581" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:46px;">current conditions and forecasts.<div style="display:inline-block;width:14px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a39591" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:77px;">The methodology for estimating the amount of credit losses reported in<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the allowance for credit losses has two basic components: </div><div id="a39631" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:184px;">Loans that do not share similar risk characteristics are evaluated on an individual<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>basis.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Loans deemed to be collateral dependent </div><div id="a39776" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:199px;">have differing risk characteristics and are individually<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>analyzed to Roman';left:4px;top:215px;">dependent when the borrower is experiencing financial difficulty<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and repayment of the loan is dependent on the liquidation and </div><div id="a39850" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:230px;">sale of the underlying collateral.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>For collateral dependent loans where foreclosure is probable, the expected<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>credit loss is </div><div id="a39886" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:245px;">measured based on the difference between the fair<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>value of the collateral (less selling cost) and the amortized cost basis of the </div><div id="a39930" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the Company has elected the practical expedient allowed </div><div id="a39966" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:276px;">by Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;)<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;) Topic<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>326-20 to measure the </div><div id="a40000" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:291px;">expected credit loss under the same approach as those loans where foreclosure<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>is probable.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>For loans with balances greater than </div><div id="a40040" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:307px;">$250,000,<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div>the fair value of the collateral is obtained through independent appraisal of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the underlying collateral.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>For loans with </div><div id="a40079" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:322px;">balances less than $250,000, the Company has made a policy election to<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>measure expected loss for these individual loans utilizing </div><div id="a40119" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:337px;">loss rates for similar loan types.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a40133" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:4px;top:368px;">Loans That Share Similar Risk Characteristics (Pooled<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Loans) </div><div id="a40150" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:399px;">The general steps in determining expected credit losses for the pooled<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>loan component of the allowance are as follows: </div><div id="a40189" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:28px;top:430px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a40191" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:52px;top:430px;">Segment loans into pools according to similar risk characteristics </div><div id="a40209" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:28px;top:447px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a40211" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:52px;top:447px;">Develop historical loss rates for each loan pool segment </div><div id="a40229" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:28px;top:463px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a40231" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:52px;top:463px;">Incorporate the impact of forecasts </div><div id="a40241" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:28px;top:479px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a40243" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:52px;top:479px;">Incorporate the impact of other qualitative factors<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a40258" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:28px;top:495px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a40260" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:52px;top:495px;">Calculate and review pool specific allowance for credit loss estimate </div><div id="a40281" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:526px;">A discounted cash flow methodology is utilized to calculate expected<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>cash flows for the life of each individual loan.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>The </div><div id="a40321" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:542px;">discounted present value of expected cash flow is then compared<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to the loan&#8217;s amortized cost basis to determine<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the credit loss </div><div id="a40363" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:557px;">estimate.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Individual loan results are aggregated at the pool level in determining<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>total reserves for each loan pool.<div style="display:inline-block;width:20px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a40401" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:587px;">The primary inputs used to calculate expected cash flows include historical<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>loss rates which reflect probability of default (&#8220;PD&#8221;) </div><div id="a40439" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:603px;">and loss given default (&#8220;LGD&#8221;), and prepayment rates.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>The historical look-back period is a key factor in the calculation of the PD </div><div id="a40485" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:618px;">rate and is based on management&#8217;s assessment<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of current and forecasted conditions and may vary by loan pool.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>Loans subject to </div><div id="a40527" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:634px;">the Company&#8217;s risk rating process are<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>further sub-segmented by risk rating in the calculation of PD rates.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>LGD rates generally </div><div id="a40569" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:649px;">reflect the historical average net loss rate by loan pool.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>Expected cash flows are further adjusted to incorporate the impact of loan </div><div id="a40613" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:664px;">prepayments which will vary by loan segment and interest rate conditions.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>In general, prepayment rates are based on observed </div><div id="a40651" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:679px;">prepayment rates occurring in the loan portfolio and consideration of forecasted<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>interest rates. </div></div></div></ix:continuation></div></div></ix:continuation></div></div>

style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:15px;">In developing loss rates, adjustments are made to incorporate the impact<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of forecasted conditions.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Certain assumptions are also </div><div id="a40717" style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>The forecast period is the period within which management is </div><div id="a40757" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:46px;">able to make a reasonable and supportable assessment of future conditions.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>The reversion period is the period beyond are periodically evaluated and based on management&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>assessment of current and forecasted conditions and </div><div id="a40913" forecast, with </div><div id="a40983" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:138px;">the forecasted unemployment rate being a significant factor.<div other risk factors that impact loan<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>defaults and losses.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>These adjustments are based </div><div id="a41151" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:230px;">on management&#8217;s assessment of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>trends and conditions that impact credit risk and resulting credit losses, more<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>specifically internal </div><div id="a41187" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:245px;">and external factors that are independent of and not reflected in the quantitative<div Roman';left:4px;top:276px;">loan review systems, collateral valuations, concentrations, legal/regulatory/political<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>conditions, and the unforeseen impact of </div><div id="a41283" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:291px;">natural disasters. </div><div id="a41288" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New sheet credit exposures is adjusted as a provision<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>for credit loss expense and is recorded in other </div><div id="a41427" that funding<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>will occur and an estimate of expected credit losses </div><div id="a41465" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New for current </div><div id="a41507" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:429px;">outstanding loan balances by segment.<div See Note 21 &#8211; Commitments </div><div id="a41583" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:460px;">and Contingencies for additional information.</div></div></div></ix:continuation></div><div id="TextContainer101" style="position:relative;width:712px;z-index:1;"></div><div id="div_98_XBRL_TS_a3f74ba4f755440eac6e4becc81e38b2" style="position:absolute;left:0px;top:491px;float:left;"><ix:nonNumeric id="ID_1114" name="us-gaap:LoansAndLeasesReceivableMortgageBankingActivitiesPolicy" contextRef="FROM_Jan01_2025_TO_Dec31_2025_Entity_0000726601" continuedAt="XBRL_TS_a3f74ba4f755440eac6e4becc81e38b2_1" escape="true"><div id="TextBlockContainer99" style="position:relative;line-height:normal;width:712px;height:461px;"><div id="TextContainer99" style="position:relative;width:712px;z-index:1;"><div id="a41595" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:4px;top:0px;">Mortgage Banking Activities </div><div id="a41602" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:4px;top:31px;">Mortgage Loans Held for Sale and Revenue Recognition </div><div id="a41619" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:61px;">Mortgage loans held for sale (&#8220;HFS&#8221;) are carried at fair value under the fair value<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>option with changes in fair value recorded in </div><div id="a41665" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:77px;">mortgage banking revenues on the Consolidated Statements of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Income. The fair value of mortgage loans held for sale committed </div><div id="a41706" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:92px;">to investors is calculated using observable market information such<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>as the investor commitment, assignment of trade or other </div><div id="a41742" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:107px;">mandatory delivery commitment prices. The Company bases loans<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>committed to Federal National Mortgage Association </div><div id="a41770" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:123px;">(&#8220;FNMA&#8221;), Government National Mortgage Association (&#8220;GNMA&#8221;),<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (&#8220;Agency&#8221;) </div><div id="a41791" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:138px;">investors based on the Agency&#8217;s quoted<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>mortgage backed security (&#8220;MBS&#8221;) prices. The fair value of mortgage loans held for<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>sale </div><div id="a41835" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:153px;">not committed to investors is based on quoted best execution secondary<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>market prices. If no such quoted price exists, the fair </div><div id="a41877" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:169px;">value is determined using quoted prices for a similar asset or assets, such as MBS prices,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>adjusted for the specific attributes of that </div><div id="a41923" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:184px;">loan, which would be used by other market participants. </div><div id="a41942" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:215px;">Gains and losses from the sale of mortgage loans held for sale are recognized based<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>upon the difference between the sales </div><div id="a41984" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:230px;">proceeds and carrying value of the related loans upon sale and are recorded<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in mortgage banking revenues on the Consolidated </div><div id="a42025" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:245px;">Statements of Income. If the related mortgage loan is sold with servicing retained, the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>MSR addition is recorded in mortgage banking revenues </div><div id="a42107" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:276px;">on the Consolidated Statements of Income.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>Mortgage banking revenues also includes the unrealized gains and losses associated </div><div id="a42145" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:291px;">with the changes in the fair value of mortgage loans held for sale, and the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>realized and unrealized gains and losses from derivative </div><div id="a42191" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:307px;">instruments. </div><div id="a42194" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:337px;">Mortgage loans held for sale are considered sold when the Company surrenders<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>control over the financial assets. Control is </div><div id="a42232" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:353px;">considered to have been surrendered when the transferred assets have been<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>isolated from the Company, beyond<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the reach of the </div><div id="a42272" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:368px;">Company and its creditors; the purchaser obtains the right (free of conditions<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>that constrain it from taking advantage of that right) </div><div id="a42314" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:383px;">to pledge or exchange the transferred assets; and the Company does not<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>maintain effective control over the transferred assets </div><div id="a42352" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:399px;">through either an agreement that both entitles and obligates the Company<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to repurchase or redeem the transferred assets before </div><div id="a42390" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:414px;">their maturity or the ability to unilaterally cause the holder to return specific<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>assets. The Company typically considers the above </div><div id="a42430" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:429px;">criteria to have been met upon acceptance and receipt of sales proceeds<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>from the purchaser. </div></div></div></ix:nonNumeric></div></div></ix:continuation></div></div>

id="TextBlockContainer108" style="position:relative;line-height:normal;width:712px;height:814px;"><div id="div_105_XBRL_TS_a3f74ba4f755440eac6e4becc81e38b2_1" style="position:relative;line-height:normal;width:712px;height:798px;"><div id="TextContainer106" style="position:relative;width:712px;z-index:1;"><div id="a42464" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:0px;">GNMA optional repurchase programs allow financial institutions to buy<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>back individual delinquent mortgage loans that meet </div><div id="a42467" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:15px;">certain criteria from the securitized loan pool for which the institution provides servicing.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>At the servicer&#8217;s authorization, the servicer may repurchase such a delinquent<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>loan for an amount equal to 100 percent of the </div><div id="a42473" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:77px;">Company is deemed to have regained effective control<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>over these loans under the unconditional buy-back option, the loans can<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>no </div><div id="a42491" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New the buy-back option.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>These loans are reported in other assets with the offsetting liability<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>being </div><div id="a42514" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:123px;">reported in other liabilities.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a42518" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:4px;top:153px;">Derivative Instruments (IRLC/Forward Commitments)</div><div id="a42527" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:184px;">The Company holds and issues derivative financial instruments such as interest<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>rate lock commitments (&#8220;IRLCs&#8221;) and other </div><div id="a42565" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:199px;">forward sale commitments. IRLCs are subject to price risk primarily<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>related to fluctuations in market interest rates. To<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>hedge the </div><div id="a42605" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:215px;">interest rate risk on certain IRLCs, the Company uses forward sale commitments,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>such as to-be-announced securities (&#8220;TBAs&#8221;) or </div><div id="a42649" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:230px;">mandatory delivery commitments with investors. Management<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>expects these forward sale commitments to experience changes in </div><div id="a42679" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:245px;">fair value opposite to the changes in fair value of the IRLCs thereby reducing<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>earnings volatility. Forward<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>sale commitments are </div><div id="a42719" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:261px;">also used to hedge the interest rate risk on mortgage loans held for sale that<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>are not committed to investors and still subject to </div><div id="a42767" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:276px;">price risk. If the mandatory delivery commitments are not fulfilled, the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Company pays a pair-off fee. Best effort<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>forward sale </div><div id="a42809" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:291px;">commitments are also executed with investors, whereby certain loans<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>are locked with a borrower and simultaneously committed </div><div id="a42843" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:307px;">to an investor at a fixed price. If the best effort IRLC does not fund,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>there is no obligation to fulfill the investor commitment. </div><div id="a42892" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:337px;">The Company considers various factors and strategies in determining<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>what portion of the IRLCs and uncommitted mortgage loans </div><div id="a42928" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:353px;">held for sale to economically hedge.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>All derivative instruments are recognized as other assets or other liabilities on<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the </div><div id="a42967" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:368px;">Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition at their fair value.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Changes in the fair value of the derivative instruments are </div><div id="a43009" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:383px;">recognized in mortgage banking revenues on the Consolidated Statements<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of Income in the period in which they occur.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Gains and </div><div id="a43052" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:399px;">losses resulting from the pairing-out of forward sale commitments are<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>recognized in mortgage banking revenues on the </div><div id="a43088" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:414px;">Consolidated Statements of Income. The Company accounts for<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>all derivative instruments as free-standing derivative instruments </div><div id="a43123" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:429px;">and does not designate any for hedge accounting. </div><div id="a43140" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:4px;top:460px;">Mortgage Servicing Rights (&#8220;MSRs&#8221;) and Revenue Recognition<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a43156" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:491px;">The Company sells residential mortgage loans in the secondary market and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>may retain the right to service the loans sold. Upon </div><div id="a43198" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:506px;">sale, an MSR asset is capitalized, which represents the then current fair value of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>future net cash flows expected to be realized for </div><div id="a43244" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:521px;">performing servicing activities.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>As the Company has not elected to subsequently measure any class of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>servicing assets under the </div><div id="a43282" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:537px;">fair value measurement method, the Company follows the amortization<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>method.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>MSRs are amortized to noninterest income </div><div id="a43314" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:552px;">(other income) in proportion to and over the period of estimated net servicing<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>income and are assessed for impairment at each </div><div id="a43356" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:567px;">reporting date.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>MSRs are carried at the lower of the initial capitalized amount, net of accumulated amortization,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or estimated fair </div><div id="a43396" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:583px;">value, and included in other assets, net, on the Consolidated Statements of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Financial Condition.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a43430" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:613px;">The Company periodically evaluates its MSRs asset for impairment.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>Impairment is assessed based on fair value at each reporting </div><div id="a43468" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:629px;">date using estimated prepayment speeds of the underlying mortgage<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>loans serviced and stratifications based on the risk </div><div id="a43502" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:644px;">characteristics of the underlying loans (predominantly loan type and note<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>interest rate).<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>As mortgage interest rates fall, </div><div id="a43536" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:659px;">prepayment speeds are usually faster and the value of the MSRs asset generally<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>decreases, requiring additional valuation reserve.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a43572" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:675px;">Conversely, as mortgage<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>interest rates rise, prepayment speeds are usually slower and the value of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the MSRs asset generally </div><div id="a43610" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:690px;">increases, requiring less valuation reserve.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>A valuation allowance is established, through a charge to earnings,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to the extent the </div><div id="a43648" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:705px;">amortized cost of the MSRs exceeds the estimated fair value by stratification.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>If it is later determined that all or a portion of the </div><div id="a43696" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:721px;">temporary impairment no longer exists for a stratification, the valuation<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>is reduced through a recovery to earnings.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>An other-than-</div><div id="a43736" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:736px;">temporary impairment (i.e., recoverability is considered remote when<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>considering interest rates and loan pay off activity) is </div><div id="a43770" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:751px;">recognized as a write-down of the MSRs asset and the related valuation allowance<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>(to the extent a valuation allowance is </div><div id="a43812" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:767px;">available) and then against earnings.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>A direct write-down permanently reduces the carrying value of the MSRs asset and </div><div id="a43850" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:782px;">valuation allowance, precluding subsequent recoveries. See Note 4 &#8211;<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Mortgage Banking Activities for additional information.</div></div></div></ix:continuation></div><div id="TextContainer108" style="position:relative;width:712px;z-index:1;"><div id="a43850_123_2" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:675px;top:782px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:3px">&#160;</div></div></div></div></ix:continuation></div></div>

<div id="a43883" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:404px;top:1022px;">85 </div><div id="div_110_XBRL_TS_6484924d0af44320be023e05797bd020_5" style="position:absolute;left:58px;top:48px;float:left;"><ix:continuation id="XBRL_TS_6484924d0af44320be023e05797bd020_5" continuedAt="XBRL_TS_6484924d0af44320be023e05797bd020_6"><div id="TextBlockContainer120" style="position:relative;line-height:normal;width:713px;height:935px;"><div id="div_111_XBRL_TS_9ef92441e92343efb4cd68ef725378ca" style="position:absolute;left:0px;top:0px;float:left;"><ix:nonNumeric id="ID_1116" name="us-gaap:DerivativesPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="FROM_Jan01_2025_TO_Dec31_2025_Entity_0000726601" escape="true"><div id="TextBlockContainer112" style="position:relative;line-height:normal;width:713px;height:460px;"><div id="TextContainer112" style="position:relative;width:713px;z-index:1;"><div id="a43885" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:4px;top:0px;">Derivative/Hedging Activities </div><div id="a43890" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:31px;">At the inception of a derivative contract, the Company designates the derivative<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>as one of three types based on the Company&#8217;s </div><div id="a43934" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:46px;">intentions and belief as to the likely effectiveness as a hedge. These<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>three types are (1) a hedge of the fair value of a recognized </div><div id="a43984" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:61px;">asset or liability or of an unrecognized firm commitment (&#8220;fair value<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>hedge&#8221;), (2) a hedge of a forecasted transaction or the </div><div id="a44030" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:77px;">variability of cash flows to be received or paid related to a recognized<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>asset or liability (&#8220;cash flow hedge&#8221;), or (3) an instrument </div><div id="a44080" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:92px;">with no hedging designation (&#8220;standalone derivative&#8221;). For a fair value hedge,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the gain or loss on the derivative, as well as the </div><div id="a44128" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:107px;">offsetting loss or gain on the hedged item, are recognized<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in current earnings as fair values change. For a cash flow hedge, the </div><div id="a44174" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:123px;">gain or loss on the derivative is reported in other comprehensive income<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and is reclassified into earnings in the same periods </div><div id="a44216" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:138px;">during which the hedged transaction affects earnings.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>For both types of hedges, changes in the fair value of derivatives that are </div><div id="a44258" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:153px;">not highly effective in hedging the changes in fair value<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or expected cash flows of the hedged item are recognized immediately in </div><div id="a44302" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:169px;">current earnings. Net cash settlements on derivatives that qualify for<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>hedge accounting are recorded in interest income or interest </div><div id="a44340" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:184px;">expense, based on the item being hedged. Net cash settlements on derivatives<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>that do not qualify for hedge accounting are </div><div id="a44380" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:199px;">reported in non-interest income. Cash flows on hedges are classified in the cash flow<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>statement the same as the cash flows of the </div><div id="a44428" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:215px;">items being hedged. </div><div id="a44435" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:245px;">The Company formally documents the relationship between derivatives<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>and hedged items, as well as the risk-management </div><div id="a44469" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:261px;">objective and the strategy for undertaking hedge transactions at the inception<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of the hedging relationship. This documentation </div><div id="a44503" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:276px;">includes linking fair value or cash flow hedges to specific assets and liabilities on<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the Consolidated Statement of Financial </div><div id="a44543" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:291px;">Condition or to specific firm commitments or forecasted transactions. The<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Company also formally assesses, both at the hedge&#8217;s </div><div id="a44582" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:307px;">inception and on an ongoing basis, whether the derivative instruments that are<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>used are highly effective in offsetting changes in </div><div id="a44622" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:322px;">fair values or cash flows of the hedged items. The Company discontinues<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>hedge accounting when it determines that the derivative </div><div id="a44662" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:337px;">is no longer effective in offsetting changes in the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>fair value or cash flows of the hedged item, the derivative is settled or </div><div id="a44708" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:353px;">terminates, a hedged forecasted transaction is no longer probable, a hedged<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>firm commitment is no longer firm, or treatment of the </div><div id="a44750" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:368px;">derivative as a hedge is no longer appropriate or intended. When hedge<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>accounting is discontinued, subsequent changes in fair </div><div id="a44788" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:383px;">value of the derivative are recorded as non-interest income. When<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a fair value hedge is discontinued, the hedged asset or liability </div><div id="a44832" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:399px;">is no longer adjusted for changes in fair value,<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div>and the existing basis adjustment is amortized or accreted over the remaining life </div><div id="a44877" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:414px;">of the asset or liability.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>When a cash flow hedge is discontinued but the hedged cash flows or forecasted<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>transactions are still </div><div id="a44921" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:429px;">expected to occur, gains or losses that were accumulated<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in other comprehensive income are amortized into earnings over the </div><div id="a44959" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:445px;">same periods, in which the hedged transactions will affect<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>earnings. <div id="TextContainer307" style="position:relative;width:710px;z-index:1;"><div id="a57154" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:0px;">Substandard &#8211; Loans in this category exhibit well-defined weaknesses that would<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>typically bring normal repayment into jeopardy. </div><div id="a57190" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:15px;">These loans are no longer adequately protected due to well-defined<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>weaknesses that affect the repayment capacity of the </div><div id="a57228" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:31px;">borrower.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>The possibility of loss is much more evident and above average supervision is required<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>for these loans. </div><div id="a57265" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:61px;">Doubtful &#8211; style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>any condition established in </div><div id="a69992" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:15px;">the contract. Commitments generally have fixed expiration dates or other<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>termination clauses and may require payment of a fee. </div><div id="a69994" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:31px;">Since many of the commitments are expected to expire without being drawn<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>upon, the total commitment amounts do not </div><div id="a69995" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:46px;">necessarily represent future cash requirements. </div><div id="a69998" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:74px;">Standby letters of credit are conditional commitments issued by the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Company to guarantee the performance of a client to a third </div><div id="a70000" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:89px;">party.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>The credit risk involved in issuing letters of credit is essentially the same as that involved<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>in extending loan facilities. In </div><div id="a70004" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:104px;">general, management does not anticipate any material losses as a result of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>participating in these types of transactions.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>However, </div><div id="a70007" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:120px;">any potential losses arising from such transactions are reserved for in the same manner<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>as management reserves for their other </div><div id="a70011" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:135px;">credit facilities. </div><div id="a70014" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:163px;">For both on- and off-balance sheet financial instruments, the Company<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>requires collateral to support such instruments when it is </div><div id="a70020" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:178px;">deemed necessary.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>The Company evaluates each client&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>creditworthiness on a case-by-case basis.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>The amount of collateral </div><div id="a70029" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:193px;">obtained upon extension of credit is based on management&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>credit evaluation of the counterparty.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>Collateral held varies but </div><div id="a70032" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:209px;">may include deposits held in financial institutions; U.S. Treasury<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>securities; other marketable securities; real estate; accounts </div><div id="a70034" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:224px;">receivable; property,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>plant and equipment; and inventory. </div><div id="a70037" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:252px;">The allowance for credit losses for off-balance sheet credit commitments<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>that are not unconditionally cancellable by the Bank is </div><div id="a70043" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:267px;">adjusted as a provision for credit loss expense and is recorded in other liabilities.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>The following table shows the activity in the </div><div id="a70047" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:282px;">allowance.</div></div></div></ix:continuation></div><div id="a70047_10_2" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:120px;top:952px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:3px">&#160;</div></div></div>

style="position:relative;width:712px;z-index:1;"><div id="a70185" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:4px;top:0px;">Note 22 </div><div id="a70188" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:4px;top:15px;">FAIR VALUE<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>MEASUREMENTS</div><div id="a70191" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:46px;">The fair value of an asset or liability is the exchange price that would be received<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>were the Bank to sell that asset or paid to </div><div id="a70200" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:61px;">transfer that liability (exit price) in an orderly transaction occurring in the principal<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>market (or most advantageous market in the </div><div id="a70203" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:77px;">absence of a principal market) for such asset or liability.<div style="display:inline-block;width:9px">&#160;</div>In estimating fair value, the Company utilizes valuation techniques that </div><div id="a70205" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:92px;">are consistent with the market approach, the income approach and/or<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the cost approach.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Such valuation techniques are </div><div id="a70206" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:107px;">consistently applied.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>Inputs to valuation techniques include the assumptions that market participants would<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>use in pricing an asset </div><div id="a70208" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:123px;">or liability.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px">&#160;</div>ASC Topic 820 establishes a fair value<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>hierarchy for valuation inputs that gives the highest priority to quoted prices </div><div id="a70211" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:138px;">in active markets for identical assets or liabilities and the lowest priority to unobservable<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>inputs.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>The fair value hierarchy is as </div><div id="a70213" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:153px;">follows: </div><div id="a70216" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:28px;top:185px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a70218" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:52px;top:185px;">Level 1 Inputs - </div><div id="a70223" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:139px;top:185px;">Unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities that the reporting<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>entity has </div><div id="a70224" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:52px;top:200px;">the ability to access at the measurement date</div><div id="a70225" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:290px;top:200px;">.</div><div id="a70228" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:28px;top:232px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a70230" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:52px;top:232px;">Level 2 Inputs - </div><div id="a70235" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:139px;top:232px;">Inputs other than quoted prices included in Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability,<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>either </div><div id="a70238" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:52px;top:247px;">directly or indirectly.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>These might include quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, quoted prices </div><div id="a70239" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:52px;top:263px;">for identical or similar assets or liabilities in markets that are not active,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>inputs other than quoted prices that are </div><div id="a70240" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:52px;top:278px;">observable for the asset or liability (such as interest rates, volatilities, prepayment<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>speeds, credit risks, etc.) or inputs that </div><div id="a70243" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:52px;top:293px;">are derived principally from, or corroborated, by market data by correlation<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>or other means</div><div id="a70244" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:538px;top:293px;">.</div><div id="a70247" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:28px;top:325px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a70249" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:52px;top:325px;">Level 3 Inputs - </div><div id="a70254" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:139px;top:325px;">Unobservable inputs for determining the fair values of assets or liabilities that reflect an<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>entity&#8217;s own </div><div id="a70257" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:52px;top:340px;">assumptions about the assumptions that market participants would<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>use in pricing the assets or liabilities. style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:4px;top:276px;">Loans Held for Sale</div><div id="a70305" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:112px;top:276px;">. The fair value of residential mortgage loans held for sale based on Level 2 inputs is determined,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>when </div><div id="a70306" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:291px;">possible, using either quoted secondary-market prices or investor commitments.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>If no such quoted price exists, the fair value is </div><div id="a70309" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:307px;">determined using quoted prices for a similar asset or assets, adjusted for<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the specific attributes of that loan, which would be used </div><div id="a70311" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:322px;">by other market participants. The Company has elected the fair value option<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>accounting for its held for sale loans.<div style="display:inline-block;width:4px">&#160;</div></div><div id="a70314" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:4px;top:353px;">Mortgage Banking Derivative Instruments. </div><div id="a70315" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:237px;top:353px;">The fair values of IRLCs are derived by valuation models incorporating<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>market </div><div id="a70319" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:368px;">pricing for instruments with similar characteristics, commonly referred<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>to as best execution pricing, or investor commitment </div><div id="a70320" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:383px;">prices for best effort IRLCs which have unobservable inputs, such as an<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>estimate of the fair value of the servicing rights expected </div><div id="a70322" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:399px;">to be recorded upon sale of the loans, net estimated costs to originate the loans, and the pull-through<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>rate, and are therefore </div><div id="a70325" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:414px;">classified as Level 3 within the fair value hierarchy.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>The fair value of forward sale commitments is based on observable market </div><div id="a70327" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:429px;">pricing for similar instruments and are therefore classified as Level 2 within<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the fair value hierarchy. </div><div id="a70330" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:4px;top:460px;">Interest Rate Swap. </div><div id="a70331" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:112px;top:460px;">The Company&#8217;s derivative positions are<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>classified as Level 2 within the fair value hierarchy and are valued </div><div id="a70334" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:475px;">using models generally accepted in the financial services industry and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>that use actively quoted or observable market input values </div><div id="a70336" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:491px;">from external market data providers. The fair value derivatives are determined<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>using discounted cash flow models. </div><div id="a70339" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:4px;top:521px;">Fair Value<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Swap</div><div id="a70340" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:537px;">valuation represents the amount due and payable to the counterparty based upon<div style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:552px;">the period.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px">&#160;</div>There was $</div><div id="a70345_24_3" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:438px;top:232px;">Our management is responsible for establishing and </div><div id="a72728" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:248px;">maintaining effective internal control over financial<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>reporting (as such term is defined in Rule 13a-15(f) under the control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>assurance regarding </div><div id="a72733" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:278px;">the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements<div financial reporting cannot provide absolute assurance<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of achieving financial reporting objectives because of </div><div id="a72740" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:340px;">its inherent limitations. Internal control over financial reporting is a process<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>that involves human diligence and compliance and is </div><div id="a72743" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:355px;">subject to lapses in judgment and breakdowns resulting from human failures.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>Internal control over financial reporting can also be </div><div id="a72745" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:370px;">circumvented by collusion or improper management override. Because of such<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>limitations, there is a risk that material </div><div id="a72746" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:386px;">misstatements may not be prevented or detected on a timely basis by internal<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>control over financial reporting. However, these </div><div id="a72748" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:401px;">inherent limitations are known features of the financial reporting<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>process. Therefore, it is possible to design into the process </div><div id="a72750" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:416px;">safeguards to reduce, though not eliminate, this risk. </div><div id="a72753" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:447px;">Management is also responsible for the preparation and fair presentation<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of the consolidated financial statements and other </div><div id="a72754" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:462px;">financial information contained in this report. We </div><div id="a72849" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:611px;">believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion. </div><div id="a72851" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:62px;top:643px;">Definitions and Limitations of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting </div><div id="a72853" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:674px;">A company&#8217;s internal control over<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>the </div><div id="a72854" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:689px;">reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of reliable consolidated<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>financial statements in accordance with accounting </div><div id="a72856" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:704px;">principles generally accepted in the United States of America. A company&#8217;s<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px">&#160;</div>internal control over financial reporting includes </div><div id="a72858" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:720px;">those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect </div><div id="a72860" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:735px;">the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as </div><div id="a72862" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:751px;">necessary to permit preparation of consolidated financial statements in<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>accordance with accounting principles generally accepted </div><div id="a72864" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:766px;">in the United States of America, and that receipts and expenditures of the<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>company are being made only in accordance with </div><div id="a72865" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:781px;">authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>reasonable assurance regarding prevention, or timely </div><div id="a72867" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:796px;">detection and correction of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>of the company&#8217;s assets that could have<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>a material effect </div><div id="a72869" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:812px;">on the consolidated financial statements. </div><div id="a72872" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:843px;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, </div><div id="a72874" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:858px;">projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate </div><div id="a72875" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:62px;top:873px;">because of changes in conditions or that the degree of compliance with the policies or<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px">&#160;</div>procedures may deteriorate. </div><div id="a72878" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:904px;">/s/ Forvis Mazars, LLP </div><div id="a72881" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:919px;">Little Rock, Arkansas </div><div id="a72883" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:62px;top:935px;">February 27, 2026</div></div>
